title.zh: 卷504 列傳二百九十一 艺術三
title.raw: 卷504 列傳二百九十一 艺術三

sentences.zh: 王時敏族侄鑑子撰孫原祁原祁曾孫宸

translations.literal: Wang Shimin; his clan nephew Jian; his grandson Yuanqi; Yuanqi's great-grandson Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shimin, his clan nephew Wang Jian, his grandson Sun Yuanqi, and Yuanqi's great-grandson Wang Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳洪綬崔子忠禹之鼎余集改琦費丹旭

translations.literal: Chen Hongshou, Cui Zizhong, Yu Zhiding, Yu Ji, Gai Qi, Fei Danxu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hongshou, Cui Zizhong, Yu Zhiding, Yu Ji, Gai Qi, and Fei Danxu.

sentences.zh: 釋道濟髡殘硃耷弘仁王翬吳歷楊晉黃鼎方士庶

translations.literal: The monk Daoji, Kun Can, Zhu Da, Hongren, Wang Hui, Wu Li, Yang Jin, Huang Ding, Fang Shidu.
translations.idiomatic: Shitao (Daoji), Kun Can, Bada Shanren, Hongren, Wang Hui, Wu Li, Yang Jin, Huang Ding, and Fang Shidu.

sentences.zh: 惲格馬元馭王武沈銓龔賢趙左項聖謨查士標

translations.literal: Yun Ge, Ma Yuanyu, Wang Wu, Shen Quan, Gong Xian, Zhao Zuo, Xiang Shengmo, Zha Shibiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Shouping, Ma Yuanyu, Wang Wu, Shen Quan, Gong Xian, Zhao Zuo, Xiang Shengmo, and Zha Shibiao.

sentences.zh: 高其佩李世倬硃倫瀚張鵬翀

translations.literal: Gao Qipei, Li Shizhuo, Zhu Lunhan, Zhang Pengchong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qipei, Li Shizhuo, Zhu Lunhan, and Zhang Pengchong.

sentences.zh: 唐岱焦秉貞郎世寧張宗蒼余省金廷標丁觀鵬繆炳泰

translations.literal: Tang Dai, Jiao Bingzhen, Lang Shining, Zhang Zongcang, Yu Sheng, Jin Tingbiao, Ding Guanpeng, Miu Bingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Dai, Jiao Bingzhen, Giuseppe Castiglione (Lang Shining), Zhang Zongcang, Yu Sheng, Jin Tingbiao, Ding Guanpeng, and Miu Bingtai.

sentences.zh: 華嵒高鳳翰鄭燮金農羅聘奚岡錢杜方薰

translations.literal: Hua Yan, Gao Fenggan, Zheng Xie, Jin Nong, Luo Pin, Xi Gang, Qian Du, Fang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yan, Gao Fenggan, Zheng Xie, Jin Nong, Luo Pin, Xi Gang, Qian Du, and Fang Xun.

sentences.zh: 王學浩黃均

translations.literal: Wang Xuehao, Huang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuehao and Huang Jun.

sentences.zh: 王時敏，字遜之，號煙客，江南太倉人，明大學士錫爵孫。

translations.literal: Wang Shimin, styled Xunzhi, sobriquet Yanke, a man of Taicang in Jiangnan, grandson of the Ming Grand Secretary Wang Xijue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shimin, whose style name was Xunzhi and sobriquet Yanke, came from Taicang in Jiangnan and was a grandson of the Ming Grand Secretary Wang Xijue.

sentences.zh: 以廕官至太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he reached office as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Through yin privilege he rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時敏係出高門，文采早著。

translations.literal: Shimin sprang from a great house, and his literary talent was early manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin was born into a distinguished family and showed literary gifts from an early age.

sentences.zh: 鼎革後，家居不出，獎掖後進，名德為時所重。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change he lived at home and did not go out, encouraged those who came after him, and his fame and virtue were heavily regarded in the age.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Ming he remained at home, mentored younger artists, and was widely esteemed for his reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 明季畫學，董其昌有開繼之功，時敏少時親炙，得其真傳。

translations.literal: In late-Ming painting studies Dong Qichang had the merit of opening and continuing the tradition; in youth Shimin received his close instruction and obtained his true transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In late-Ming painting Dong Qichang had pioneered the renewal of the tradition; Shimin studied under him in youth and received the authentic lineage.

sentences.zh: 錫爵晚而抱孫，彌鍾愛，居之別業，廣收名跡，悉窮秘奧。

translations.literal: Xijue, late in life, embraced a grandson and loved him ever more; he had him dwell in a separate estate, widely collected famous traces, and thoroughly exhausted their hidden subtleties.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue, in his old age, doted on this grandson, settled him in a separate estate, amassed celebrated works of art, and explored their deepest secrets with him.

sentences.zh: 於黃公望墨法，尤有深契，暮年益臻神化。

translations.literal: In Huang Gongwang's ink method he had especially deep affinity; in his late years he increasingly reached divine transformation.
translations.idiomatic: He felt a profound affinity with Huang Gongwang's ink manner, and in his later years his art approached sublime mastery.

sentences.zh: 愛才若渴，四方工畫者踵接於門，得其指授，無不知名於時，為一代畫苑領袖。

translations.literal: He loved talent as though thirsty; painters skilled in the craft from the four quarters pressed in at his gate one after another, and those who received his guidance all without exception gained renown in the age—leader of the painting garden for a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Thirsting for talent, he drew skilled painters from every quarter to his door; all who studied under him won fame, and he became the leading figure of his generation in the art world.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，卒，年八十有九。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi he died, aged eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year of the Kangxi reign, at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 鑑，字圓照，明尚書世貞曾孫。

translations.literal: Jian, styled Yuanzhao, was a great-grandson of the Ming Minister Wang Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, whose style name was Yuanzhao, was a great-grandson of the Ming Minister Wang Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 與時敏同族，為子侄行，而年相若。

translations.literal: He was of the same clan as Shimin and in the nephew generation, yet their years were similar.
translations.idiomatic: He belonged to the same clan as Shimin and stood to him in the nephew generation, though the two were close in age.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，官廉州知府，甫強仕，謝職歸。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen era he served as prefect of Lianzhou; having just reached vigorous maturity, he resigned his post and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he served as prefect of Lianzhou, but while still in his prime he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 就弇園故址，營構居之，蕭然世外。

translations.literal: On the old site of the Yian Garden he built a dwelling and lived there, desolate as though beyond the world.
translations.idiomatic: On the former grounds of the Yian Garden he built a residence and lived there in lofty seclusion from the world.

sentences.zh: 與時敏砥礪畫學，以董源、巨然為宗，沈雄古逸，雖青綠重色，書味盎然。

translations.literal: With Shimin he whetted their painting studies, taking Dong Yuan and Juran as their models; deep and bold, ancient and remote—even in heavy blue-green color, the flavor of literati painting abounded.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Shimin he refined their art, taking Dong Yuan and Juran as masters; his work was grave, powerful, and archaic, and even in rich blue-green coloring it breathed the spirit of scholarly painting.

sentences.zh: 後學尊之，與時敏匹。

translations.literal: Later students revered him as a match for Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: Later painters honored him as Shimin's equal.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年，卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of Kangxi, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 孫原祁，字茂京，號麓台。

translations.literal: Sun Yuanqi, styled Maojing, sobriquet Lutai.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuanqi, whose style name was Maojing and sobriquet Lutai.

sentences.zh: 幼作山水，張齋壁，時敏見之，訝曰：「吾何時為此耶？」

translations.literal: As a child he did landscape painting and pasted it on the wall of a study room; when Shimin saw it he said in astonishment, "When did I paint this?"
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he painted landscapes and pasted them on the wall of his study; when Shimin saw them he exclaimed in surprise, "When did I paint these?"

sentences.zh: 問知，乃大奇曰：「此子業且出我右！」

translations.literal: When he learned who had done it, he said in great wonder, "This boy's accomplishment will soon surpass mine!"
translations.idiomatic: Learning who had made them, he marveled, "This child's skill will soon surpass my own!"

sentences.zh: 康熙九年成進士，授任縣知縣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Rencheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Rencheng County.

sentences.zh: 行取給事中，尋改中允，直南書房。

translations.literal: Selected for promotion to supervising secretary, soon transferred to palace bachelor, serving in the Southern Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for the capital and made a supervising secretary, then soon transferred to palace bachelor and assigned to the Southern Studio.

sentences.zh: 累擢戶部侍郎，歷官有聲。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to Vice Minister of Revenue, and in every post he held won praise.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Vice Minister of Revenue, earning a fine reputation in every office he held.

sentences.zh: 時海內清晏，聖祖右文，幾馀怡情翰墨，常召入便殿，從容奏對。

translations.literal: At the time within the seas was clear and tranquil; the sage ancestor favored literature; in spare moments he took pleasure in brush and ink, and often summoned Yuanqi into the informal hall for easy memorial replies.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was at peace and the Kangxi Emperor cherished learning; in his leisure he delighted in painting and calligraphy, and often summoned Yuanqi to the informal hall for relaxed conversation.

sentences.zh: 或於御前染翰，上憑幾觀之，不覺移晷。

translations.literal: Sometimes he painted at the imperial presence while the emperor leaned on a couch and watched, unaware of the passing of the sundial mark.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he would paint before the throne while the emperor leaned on a couch and watched, heedless of how the hours passed.

sentences.zh: 命鑑定內府名跡，充書畫譜總裁、萬壽盛典總裁，恩禮特異。

translations.literal: He was ordered to authenticate famous traces in the inner storehouse and served as general editor of the painting and calligraphy catalog and of the Wan Shou grand anthology; imperial grace and ceremony were exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with authenticating masterpieces in the imperial collection and served as chief editor of the painting and calligraphy register and of the Wan Shou ceremonial compendium, receiving extraordinary favor from the throne.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，卒於官，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he died in office, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In his fifty-fourth year he died in office, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 原祁畫為時敏親授，於黃公望淺絳法，獨有心得，晚复好用吳鎮墨法。

translations.literal: Yuanqi's painting was personally transmitted by Shimin; in Huang Gongwang's light cinnabar method he had his own understanding, and in later years he again favored Wu Zhen's ink method.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi had learned painting directly from Shimin; he developed a distinctive grasp of Huang Gongwang's light cinnabar manner and in his later years often turned to Wu Zhen's ink style.

sentences.zh: 時敏嘗曰：「元季四家，首推子久，得其神者，惟董宗伯；

translations.literal: Shimin once said, "Of the four masters of the Yuan end, Zijiu is foremost; the one who obtained his spirit is only Lord Dong;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin once remarked, "Among the Four Masters of the late Yuan, Zijiu stands first; only Lord Dong Qichang captured his spirit;

sentences.zh: 得其形者，予不敢讓；

translations.literal: the one who obtained his form—I do not dare yield;
translations.idiomatic: as for his form, I do not yield to anyone;

sentences.zh: 若形神俱得，吾孫其庶幾乎？」

translations.literal: if both form and spirit are obtained, is not my grandson perhaps close?"
translations.idiomatic: but if one could grasp both form and spirit, would not my grandson come nearest?"

sentences.zh: 王翬名傾一時，原祁高曠之致突過之。

translations.literal: Wang Hui's fame inclined the age, yet Yuanqi's lofty and spacious air suddenly surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui's fame dominated the age, yet Yuanqi's lofty, expansive manner distinctly surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 每畫必以宣德紙，重毫筆，頂煙墨，曰：「三者一不備，不足以發古雋渾逸之趣。」

translations.literal: Whenever he painted he must use Xuande paper, a heavy fine brush, and top-grade lampblack ink, saying, "If any one of the three is not prepared, it is insufficient to release the interest of ancient refinement, density, and remote ease."
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on Xuande paper, a heavy fine brush, and the finest lampblack ink for every painting, saying, "Without all three one cannot evoke the ancient flavor of refined power, density, and effortless distance."

sentences.zh: 或問王翬，曰「太熟」；

translations.literal: When asked about Wang Hui, he said, "Too mature";
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Wang Hui, he said, "Too polished";

sentences.zh: 復問查士標，曰「太生」。

translations.literal: asked again about Zha Shibiao, he said, "Too raw."
translations.idiomatic: asked about Zha Shibiao, he said, "Too raw."

sentences.zh: 蓋以不生不熟自居。

translations.literal: Thus he placed himself as neither raw nor mature.
translations.idiomatic: He thus claimed for himself the middle ground between rawness and polish.

sentences.zh: 中年後，供奉內廷，乞畫者多出代筆，而自署名。

translations.literal: After middle age, while serving in the inner court, most of those who begged paintings received works done by substitute brushes, yet he signed his own name.
translations.idiomatic: After midlife, while serving at court, most commissions were fulfilled by assistants, though he signed them himself.

sentences.zh: 每歲晏，與門下賓客畫，人一幅，為製裘之需，好事者緘金以待。

translations.literal: Every year at year's end he painted with disciples and guests beneath his gate, one painting per person, for the need of making furs; those who delighted in such things sealed gold and waited.
translations.idiomatic: At each year's end he painted one picture for every disciple and guest, to pay for new furs; enthusiasts would seal payment in advance and wait.

sentences.zh: 弟子最著者黃鼎、唐岱，並別有傳。

translations.literal: Among disciples the most renowned were Huang Ding and Tang Dai; both have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His most famous pupils were Huang Ding and Tang Dai, each of whom has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 原祁曾孫宸，字子凝，號蓬心。

translations.literal: Yuanqi's great-grandson Chen, styled Zining, sobriquet Pengxin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqi's great-grandson Wang Chen, whose style name was Zining and sobriquet Pengxin.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十五年舉人，官湖南永州知府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate and served as prefect of Yongzhou in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong and served as prefect of Yongzhou in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 原祁諸孫，多以畫世其家，惟宸最工。

translations.literal: Among Yuanqi's grandsons many handed down painting through the family, but only Chen was most skilled.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Yuanqi's descendants carried on the family tradition in painting, but Chen was the most accomplished.

sentences.zh: 枯毫重墨，氣味荒古。

translations.literal: Withered brush and heavy ink, the flavor wild and ancient.
translations.idiomatic: He used dry brush and dense ink to achieve a rugged, archaic quality.

sentences.zh: 愛永州山水，自號瀟湘子，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: He loved the mountains and waters of Yongzhou, styled himself Master Xiaoxiang, and had the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the landscape of Yongzhou, took the sobriquet Master Xiaoxiang, and intended to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 罷官後，貧不能歸，畢沅為總督，遂往依之武昌。

translations.literal: After leaving office he was poor and could not return home; Bi Yuan was governor-general, so he went to rely on him at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: After retiring from office he was too poor to go home; when Bi Yuan became governor-general he went to stay with him at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 以詩畫易酒，湖湘間尤重其畫。

translations.literal: He exchanged poems and paintings for wine; between the lakes and Xiang his paintings were especially prized.
translations.idiomatic: He traded poems and paintings for wine, and his work was especially prized throughout Hunan.

sentences.zh: 著繪林伐材十卷，王昶稱為「畫史總龜」雲。

translations.literal: He authored ten fascicles of Felling Timber in the Painting Forest; Wang Chang called it the "general tortoise of painting history."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the ten-fascicle Felling Timber in the Painting Forest, which Wang Chang hailed as the definitive compendium of painting history.

sentences.zh: 陳洪綬，字章侯，浙江諸暨人。

translations.literal: Chen Hongshou, styled Zhanghou, a man of Zhuji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hongshou, whose style name was Zhanghou, came from Zhuji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 幼適婦翁家，登案畫關壯繆像於素壁，長八九尺，婦翁見之驚異，扃室奉之。

translations.literal: In youth he went to his father-in-law's house; climbing on a table he painted an image of Lord Guan on a plain wall, eight or nine feet long; when his father-in-law saw it he was startled and amazed, locked the room and honored it.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he lived with his father-in-law; climbing on a table he painted a figure of Lord Guan on a bare wall, eight or nine feet tall; his father-in-law was astonished, sealed the room, and treasured the painting.

sentences.zh: 洪綬畫人物，衣紋清勁，力量氣局，在仇、唐之上。

translations.literal: Hongshou painted figures; garment folds were clear and forceful, strength and compositional breath above Qiu and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In figure painting his drapery lines were crisp and vigorous, and the force and scope of his compositions surpassed Qiu Ying and Tang Yin.

sentences.zh: 嘗至杭州，摹府學石刻李公麟七十二賢像，又摹周昉美人圖，數四不已，人謂其勝原本，曰：「此所以不及也。

translations.literal: He once went to Hangzhou and copied the stone-engraved images of the seventy-two worthies by Li Gonglin at the prefectural school, and also copied Zhou Fang's Beautiful Women, copying them again and again without cease; people said they surpassed the originals, and he said, "That is why they fall short.
translations.idiomatic: He once went to Hangzhou and copied Li Gonglin's stone engravings of the Seventy-Two Worthies at the prefectural school, and Zhou Fang's Beautiful Women as well, working each over and over; when people said his copies surpassed the originals, he replied, "That is precisely why they fall short.

sentences.zh: 吾畫易見好，則能事猶未盡。」

translations.literal: My paintings are easily seen as pleasing, then the full reach of skill is not yet exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: My paintings win approval too easily; that means my skill has not yet reached its limit."

sentences.zh: 嘗為諸生，崇禎間，遊京師，召為舍人，摹歷代帝王像，縱觀禦府圖畫，藝益進。

translations.literal: He had been a student; in the Chongzhen era he traveled to the capital, was summoned as attendant gentleman, copied portraits of emperors through the ages, and viewed at will paintings in the imperial storehouse; his art daily advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a licentiate; during the Chongzhen reign he went to the capital, was summoned as a court attendant, copied portraits of emperors through the ages, and studied the imperial collection, and his art steadily improved.

sentences.zh: 尋辭歸。

translations.literal: Soon he resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 鼎革後，混跡浮屠間，初號老蓮，至是自號悔遲。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change he mingled traces among Buddhist monks; at first his sobriquet was Old Lotus, and from this time he styled himself Repentant Tardiness.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic change he lived among Buddhist monks; he had earlier called himself Old Lotus, and now styled himself Repentant Tardiness.

sentences.zh: 縱酒不羈，語及亂離，輒慟哭。

translations.literal: He gave free rein to wine and was unrestrained; when speech touched on turmoil and separation he would wail in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He drank freely and lived without restraint; whenever talk turned to the chaos of the times he would burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 後數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 子字，號小蓮。

translations.literal: His son Zi, sobriquet Little Lotus.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen Zi, sobriquet Little Lotus,

sentences.zh: 畫亦有名。

translations.literal: was also famed in painting.
translations.idiomatic: was also known for his painting.

sentences.zh: 洪綬在京師與崔子忠齊名，號「南陳北崔」雲。

translations.literal: Hongshou in the capital was famed equally with Cui Zizhong, styled "Chen in the south, Cui in the north."
translations.idiomatic: In the capital Hongshou was ranked with Cui Zizhong, and the two were known as "Chen in the south, Cui in the north."

sentences.zh: 子忠，一名丹，字道母，別號青蚓，山東萊陽人，寄籍順天。

translations.literal: Zizhong, one name Dan, styled Daomu, alternate sobriquet Green Earthworm, a man of Laiyang in Shandong, with registered domicile in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zizhong, also named Dan, whose style name was Daomu and alternate sobriquet Green Earthworm, was a native of Laiyang in Shandong but registered in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，負異才。

translations.literal: He was a student and bore extraordinary talent.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he possessed rare genius.

sentences.zh: 作畫意趣在晉、唐之間，不屑襲宋、元窠臼。

translations.literal: In painting his artistic interest lay between Jin and Tang; he disdained to follow Song and Yuan rut-holes.
translations.idiomatic: His painting looked back to the Jin and Tang masters and scorned the mannerisms of Song and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 人物士女尤勝，董其昌稱之，謂非近代所有。

translations.literal: In figures and ladies he was especially superior; Dong Qichang praised him, saying such work was not possessed in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled above all in figures and court ladies; Dong Qichang praised him as unmatched in recent generations.

sentences.zh: 以金帛請者不應，家居常絕食。

translations.literal: Those who requested with gold and silk he did not answer; at home he often went without food.
translations.idiomatic: He refused commissions offered in gold and silk, and at home he often went hungry.

sentences.zh: 史可法贈以馬，售得金，呼友痛飲，一日而金盡。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa gave him a horse; he sold it for gold, called friends to drink deeply, and in one day the gold was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa gave him a horse; he sold it, summoned friends for a drinking bout, and spent every coin in a single day.

sentences.zh: 為詩古文，奧博奇崛。

translations.literal: In poetry and ancient prose he was abstruse, broad, strange, and towering.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were profound, expansive, and boldly original.

sentences.zh: 遭亂，走居土室中，遂窮餓以死。

translations.literal: Caught in turmoil, he fled to dwell in an earthen chamber and thus died in utter want and starvation.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos came he hid in an earthen hut and died of poverty and hunger.

sentences.zh: 其後畫人物士女最著者，曰禹之鼎、余集、改琦、費丹旭。

translations.literal: After him the most renowned in painting figures and ladies were called Yu Zhiding, Yu Ji, Gai Qi, and Fei Danxu.
translations.idiomatic: Later the most celebrated painters of figures and ladies were Yu Zhiding, Yu Ji, Gai Qi, and Fei Danxu.

sentences.zh: 之鼎，字尚吉，號慎齋，江蘇江都人。

translations.literal: Zhiding, styled Shangji, sobriquet Shenzhai, a man of Jiangdu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhiding, whose style name was Shangji and sobriquet Shenzhai, came from Jiangdu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 幼師藍瑛，後出入宋、元諸家，尤擅人物，繪王會圖傳世。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Lan Ying; later he moved in and out among Song and Yuan masters, especially skilled in figures; his Wang Hui Assembly has been handed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Lan Ying in youth, later absorbed Song and Yuan masters, and excelled in figure painting; his Assembly at Wang Hui's survives today.

sentences.zh: 其寫真多白描，不襲李公麟之舊，而用吳道子蘭葉法，兩顴微用脂赭染之，彌復古雅。

translations.literal: His portraits were mostly plain outline drawing; he did not follow Li Gonglin's old manner but used Wu Daozi's orchid-leaf method, lightly applying rouge and ochre to both cheekbones, ever more restoring ancient elegance.
translations.idiomatic: His portraits were mostly in plain ink line, not following Li Gonglin but using Wu Daozi's orchid-leaf brushwork, with a touch of rouge on the cheekbones for added archaic grace.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，授鴻臚寺序班。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era he was appointed protocol usher of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he was appointed a protocol usher in the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 愛洞庭山水，欲居之，遂歸。

translations.literal: He loved the mountains and waters of Dongting, wished to dwell there, and thus returned.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Dongting landscape, wished to settle there, and resigned to go home.

sentences.zh: 朝貴名流，多屬繪圖像，世每傳之。

translations.literal: Court nobles and famous men mostly commissioned him to paint portraits, and the age often transmitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials and eminent men often commissioned portraits from him, and his works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 集，字秋室，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Qiushi, a man of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ji, whose style name was Qiushi, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the thirty-first year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 工畫士女，時稱曰「余美人」，廷試，當得大魁，因此抑之。

translations.literal: Skilled in painting ladies, the age called him "Yu the Beauty"; in the palace examination he ought to have taken first place, and for this reason was held down.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at painting ladies and was nicknamed "Yu the Beauty"; in the palace examination he would have ranked first but was passed over for that reason.

sentences.zh: 尋充四庫全書纂修，薦授翰林院編修，累擢侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon he served as compiler of the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, was recommended and appointed Hanlin compiler, and rose repeatedly to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the compilation of the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries, was recommended as a Hanlin compiler, and rose to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 所作風神靜朗，無畫史氣，為世所重，比諸仇、唐遺跡。

translations.literal: What he made had spirit and bearing quiet and clear, without the air of a painting chronicler; the age prized it, comparing it to surviving traces of Qiu and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His work was serene and luminous, free of the manner of a mere artisan, and was prized as comparable to the legacy of Qiu Ying and Tang Yin.

sentences.zh: 琦，字伯蘊，號七薌，先世為西域人，壽春鎮總兵光宗孫，因家江南，居華亭。

translations.literal: Qi, styled Boyun, sobriquet Seven Fragrances; his forebears were men of the Western Regions, grandson of Guangzong, regional commander of Shouchun garrison; he then made his home in Jiangnan and dwelt in Huating.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Qi, whose style name was Boyun and sobriquet Seven Fragrances, was of Western Region descent, grandson of the Shouchun garrison commander Guangzong; his family settled in Jiangnan and lived in Huating.

sentences.zh: 琦通敏多能，工詩詞。

translations.literal: Qi was penetrating, quick, and multiply able, skilled in poetry and lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Qi was quick-witted and versatile, and accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 嘉、道後畫人物，琦號最工。

translations.literal: After Jiaqing and Daoguang in painting figures, Qi was styled most skilled.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns he was regarded as the finest figure painter of his day.

sentences.zh: 出入李公麟、趙孟頫、唐寅及近代陳洪綬諸家。

translations.literal: He moved in and out among Li Gonglin, Zhao Mengfu, Tang Yin, and recent masters such as Chen Hongshou.
translations.idiomatic: He drew on Li Gonglin, Zhao Mengfu, Tang Yin, and the recent master Chen Hongshou.

sentences.zh: 花草蘭竹小品，迥出塵表，有惲格遺意。

translations.literal: Small works of flowers, grasses, orchids, and bamboo suddenly surpassed the dust of the world, bearing traces of Yun Ge's legacy.
translations.idiomatic: His small studies of flowers, orchids, and bamboo rose above the commonplace and echoed Yun Shouping.

sentences.zh: 丹旭，字子苕，號曉樓，浙江烏程人。

translations.literal: Danxu, styled Zitiao, sobriquet Xiaolou, a man of Wucheng in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Danxu, whose style name was Zitiao and sobriquet Xiaolou, came from Wucheng in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 工寫真，如鏡取影，無不曲肖。

translations.literal: Skilled in portraiture, like a mirror taking a shadow—none not bent to likeness.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at portraiture, capturing likenesses as faithfully as a mirror.

sentences.zh: 所作士女，娟秀有神，景物佈置皆瀟灑，近世無出其右者。

translations.literal: The ladies he made were graceful and spirited; arrangement of scenery was all free and easy—in recent times none surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: His ladies were graceful and vivid, his settings elegantly composed, and in recent times none could match him.

sentences.zh: 釋道濟，字石濤，明楚籓裔，自號清湘老人。

translations.literal: The monk Daoji, styled Shitao, descendant of the Ming Prince of Chu, styled himself Old Man of Clear Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Shitao (Daoji), whose style name was Shitao and who was a descendant of the Ming Prince of Chu, called himself the Old Man of Clear Xiang.

sentences.zh: 題畫自署或曰大滌子，或曰苦瓜和尚，或曰瞎尊者，無定稱。

translations.literal: On paintings he signed himself sometimes Great Purifier, sometimes Bitter Melon Monk, sometimes Blind Honored One—no fixed title.
translations.idiomatic: He signed his paintings variously as the Great Purifier, the Bitter Melon Monk, or the Blind Honored One, with no fixed name.

sentences.zh: 國變後為僧，畫筆縱恣，脫盡窠臼，而實與古人相合。

translations.literal: After the change of dynasty he became a monk; his brush was unrestrained and free, casting off every rut, yet in truth it accorded with the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Ming he became a monk; his brushwork was bold and free of convention, yet in spirit it aligned with the ancients.

sentences.zh: 晚游江、淮，人爭重之。

translations.literal: In his late years he traveled the Yangzi and Huai; people strove to prize him.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he traveled the Yangzi and Huai regions, where his work was eagerly sought.

sentences.zh: 著論畫一卷，詞議玄妙。

translations.literal: He authored one fascicle On Painting; its words and arguments were abstruse and subtle.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a fascicle On Painting, subtle and profound in its discourse.

sentences.zh: 與髡殘齊名，號「二石」。

translations.literal: With Kun Can he was famed equally, styled the "Two Stones."
translations.idiomatic: He was ranked with Kun Can and the two were known as the "Two Stones."

sentences.zh: 髡殘，字石溪，湖南武陵人。

translations.literal: Kun Can, styled Shixi, a man of Wuling in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Kun Can, whose style name was Shixi, came from Wuling in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，自翦發投龍三三家菴。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he cut his own hair and entered the Long Sanjia Hermitage.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he shaved his own head and entered the Long Sanjia Hermitage.

sentences.zh: 遍遊名山，後至江寧，住牛首，為堂頭和尚。

translations.literal: He traveled famous mountains everywhere, later reaching Jiangning and dwelling at Niushou, becoming abbot.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled famous mountains, later settled at Niushou in Jiangning, and became abbot.

sentences.zh: 畫山水奧境奇闢，緬邈幽深，引人入勝。

translations.literal: In landscape painting his hidden realms were strange and rare, remote and deep, leading people into winning scenes.
translations.idiomatic: His landscapes opened hidden, marvelous vistas, remote and profound, that drew viewers into their depths.

sentences.zh: 道濟排奡縱橫，以奔放勝；

translations.literal: Daoji was bold and unrestrained, winning through abandon;
translations.idiomatic: Daoji painted with bold, sweeping freedom and excelled in exuberance;

sentences.zh: 髡殘沉著痛快，以謹嚴勝；

translations.literal: Kun Can was grave and exhilarating, winning through strictness;
translations.idiomatic: Kun Can was grave yet vivid and excelled in disciplined control;

sentences.zh: 皆獨絕。

translations.literal: both were utterly unique.
translations.idiomatic: each stood alone in his age.

sentences.zh: 硃耷，字雪個，江西人，亦明宗室。

translations.literal: Zhu Da, styled Xuege, a man of Jiangxi, also of Ming imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Bada Shanren (Zhu Da), whose style name was Xuege, was a Jiangxi native and also of Ming imperial descent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎甲申後，號八大山人，嘗為僧。

translations.literal: After the jiashen year of Chongzhen he styled himself Eight Great Mountain Man and once became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: After the jiashen year of Chongzhen he took the name Eight Great Mountain Man and for a time was a monk.

sentences.zh: 其書畫題款「八大」二字每聯綴，「山人」二字亦然，類「哭」類「笑」，意蓋有在。

translations.literal: On his paintings and calligraphy the two characters "Eight Great" were always joined, and "Mountain Man" likewise, resembling "cry" and resembling "laugh"—the meaning surely lay therein.
translations.idiomatic: On his paintings and calligraphy he always joined the characters for "Eight Great," and "Mountain Man" as well, forms that resemble the words for weeping and laughter—surely with intent.

sentences.zh: 畫簡略蒼勁，生動盡致，山水精密者尤妙絕，不概見。

translations.literal: His painting was brief yet forceful and vivid to the utmost; landscapes done with precision were especially marvelous and not commonly seen.
translations.idiomatic: His brushwork was spare yet powerful and vividly alive; his finely wrought landscapes were especially superb and rarely seen.

sentences.zh: 慷慨嘯歌，世以狂目之。

translations.literal: He sang and whistled freely in generous spirit; the world regarded him as mad.
translations.idiomatic: He sang and whistled with passionate abandon, and the world called him mad.

sentences.zh: 弘仁，字漸江，安徽休寧人，姓江，字亦奇。

translations.literal: Hongren, styled Jianjiang, a man of Xiuning in Anhui; surname Jiang, style name also Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongren, whose style name was Jianjiang, came from Xiuning in Anhui; his surname was Jiang and his given name Qi.

sentences.zh: 明諸生，亦甲申後為僧。

translations.literal: A Ming student, he too became a monk after the jiashen year.
translations.idiomatic: A Ming licentiate, he too became a monk after the jiashen year.

sentences.zh: 工詩古文，畫師倪瓚，新安畫家皆宗之。

translations.literal: Skilled in ancient prose and poetry, in painting he took Ni Zan as master; painters of Xin'an all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in poetry and ancient prose and studied Ni Zan in painting; the Xin'an school all looked to him.

sentences.zh: 然弘仁所作層崖陡壑，偉俊沈厚，非若世之以疏竹枯株摹擬高士者比。

translations.literal: Yet what Hongren made were layered cliffs and steep ravines, grand, lofty, deep, and heavy—not like those in the world who copy sparse bamboo and withered trees to imitate lofty recluses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his layered cliffs and steep gorges were majestic, weighty, and profound—not the sparse bamboo and withered trees with which others merely imitated recluses.

sentences.zh: 歿後，墓上種梅數百本，因稱梅花古衲雲。

translations.literal: After his death several hundred plum trees were planted on his tomb, and he was therefore called the Old Monk of Plum Blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: After his death hundreds of plum trees were planted on his grave, earning him the name Old Monk of Plum Blossoms.

sentences.zh: 自道濟以下，皆明之遺民，隱於僧，而以畫著。

translations.literal: From Daoji downward, all were remnant subjects of the Ming who hid among monks and were renowned through painting.
translations.idiomatic: From Daoji onward they were all Ming loyalists who hid as monks and won fame through painting.

sentences.zh: 其後畫僧，上睿、明中、達受最有名。

translations.literal: Among later monk-painters, Shang Rui, Mingzhong, and Dashou were most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Among later monk-painters, Shang Rui, Mingzhong, and Dashou were the most celebrated.

sentences.zh: 上睿，字目存，吳人。

translations.literal: Shang Rui, styled Mucun, a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rui, whose style name was Mucun, was a native of Wu.

sentences.zh: 嘗從王翬遊，得其指授。

translations.literal: He once traveled with Wang Hui and received his instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He once studied with Wang Hui and received his guidance.

sentences.zh: 明中，字大恆，浙江桐鄉人。

translations.literal: Mingzhong, styled Daheng, a man of Tongxiang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhong, whose style name was Daheng, came from Tongxiang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 晚主杭州南屏淨慈。

translations.literal: In his late years he presided over Jingci at Nanping in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he headed Jingci Temple at Nanping in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗南巡，賜紫衣。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor toured the south, he was granted purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor toured the south, he was granted purple monastic robes.

sentences.zh: 山水得元人法。

translations.literal: In landscape he obtained Yuan masters' method.
translations.idiomatic: His landscapes followed Yuan-dynasty methods.

sentences.zh: 達受，字六舟，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Dashou, styled Liuzhou, a man of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou, whose style name was Liuzhou, came from Haining in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 故名家子。

translations.literal: He was originally the son of a famous family.
translations.idiomatic: He came from a distinguished family.

sentences.zh: 耽翰墨，書得徐渭、陳道复縱逸之致。

translations.literal: Devoted to brush and ink, in calligraphy he obtained the free and easy spirit of Xu Wei and Chen Daofu.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to brush and ink, his calligraphy caught the uninhibited spirit of Xu Wei and Chen Daofu.

sentences.zh: 善別古器。

translations.literal: Skilled at distinguishing antiquities.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at authenticating antiquities.

sentences.zh: 精摹搨，或點綴折枝於其間，多古趣。

translations.literal: Expert at fine rubbing; sometimes he added broken branches among them, full of ancient interest.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at fine rubbings and sometimes added broken branches to them, full of archaic charm.

sentences.zh: 阮元呼曰「金石僧」。

translations.literal: Ruan Yuan called him the "Epigraphic Monk."
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan called him the Epigraphic Monk.

sentences.zh: 王翬，字石谷，號耕煙，江南常熟人。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, styled Shigu, sobriquet Gengyan, a man of Changshu in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, whose style name was Shigu and sobriquet Gengyan, came from Changshu in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 太倉王鑑遊虞山，見其畫，大驚異，索見，時年甫冠。

translations.literal: Wang Jian of Taicang traveled to Yushan, saw his paintings, was greatly startled and amazed, and asked to meet him—he was then just past the capping age.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian of Taicang visited Yushan, was astonished by his paintings, and asked to meet him when Hui was barely twenty.

sentences.zh: 載歸，謁王時敏，館之西田。

translations.literal: He took him home and presented him to Wang Shimin, who lodged him at Xitian.
translations.idiomatic: Jian brought him home and introduced him to Wang Shimin, who lodged him at Xitian.

sentences.zh: 盡出唐以後名跡，俾坐臥其中，時敏复挈之游江南北，盡得觀收藏家秘本。

translations.literal: He brought out famous traces from Tang onward and had him sit and lie among them; Shimin again took him to travel north and south of the Yangzi, fully viewing collectors' secret originals.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin brought out masterpieces from the Tang onward and had him live among them, then took him traveling north and south of the Yangzi to study collectors' hidden treasures.

sentences.zh: 如是垂二十年，學遂成。

translations.literal: Thus for nearly twenty years his learning was completed.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years his training was thus completed.

sentences.zh: 康熙中詔徵，以布衣供奉內廷。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era an edict summoned him, and as a commoner he served in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi reign he was summoned by imperial edict and served at court as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 繪南巡圖，集海內能手，逡巡莫敢下筆，翬口講指授，咫尺千里，令眾分繪而總其成。

translations.literal: To paint the Southern Tour picture, masters from within the seas were gathered; they hesitated and dared not set brush to it. Hui spoke and directed with his finger, a thousand li in a foot's span, ordering the crowd to paint in parts while he unified the whole.
translations.idiomatic: For the Southern Tour scroll the empire's finest painters were assembled, yet none dared begin; Hui directed them orally, composing a thousand li within a foot's span, assigning sections to each while unifying the whole.

sentences.zh: 圖成，聖祖稱善，欲授官，固辭，厚賜歸。

translations.literal: When the picture was finished the sage ancestor praised it and wished to grant him office; he firmly declined and was richly rewarded and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When the scroll was finished the Kangxi Emperor praised it and offered him an office; he firmly declined and returned home with rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 公卿祖餞，賦詩贈行。

translations.literal: Nobles and ministers saw him off with feasts and poems presented for his journey.
translations.idiomatic: Court nobles and ministers feasted him and presented farewell poems.

sentences.zh: 翬天性孝友，篤於風義，時敏、鑑既歿，歲時猶省其墓。

translations.literal: Hui was by nature filial and friendly and earnest in honor and duty; after Shimin and Jian had died, he still visited their graves at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was naturally filial and devoted to friendship; after Shimin and Jian died he still visited their graves each year.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十六年，卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year of Kangxi he died, aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-sixth year of Kangxi, at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 翬論畫曰：「以元人筆墨，運宋人丘壑，而澤以唐人

translations.literal: Hui said of painting: "Take Yuan people's brush and ink, deploy Song people's hills and ravines, and enrich them with Tang people's
translations.idiomatic: Hui said of painting, "Use Yuan brush and ink, Song composition in hills and ravines, and infuse them with Tang

sentences.zh: 氣韻，乃為大成。」

translations.literal: breath and resonance—only then is it great completion."
translations.idiomatic: spirit and resonance—that is true mastery."

sentences.zh: 稱之者曰：「古今筆墨之齟《齒吾》不相入者，翬羅而置之筆端，融冶以出。

translations.literal: Those who praised him said: "Brush and ink through the ages that could not fit together, Hui gathered and placed at the brush tip, smelting and bringing them forth.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said, "Brush manners through the ages that would not harmonize, Hui gathered at his brush tip and fused them into one.

sentences.zh: 畫有南、北宗，至翬而合。」

translations.literal: Painting had Southern and Northern schools; with Hui they were united."
translations.idiomatic: Painting had Southern and Northern schools; in Hui they were united."

sentences.zh: 吳歷，又名子歷，字漁山，號墨井道人，亦常熟人。

translations.literal: Wu Li, also named Zili, styled Yushan, sobriquet Mojing Daoist—also a man of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Li, also named Zili, whose style name was Yushan and sobriquet Mojing Daoist, was also from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 學畫於王時敏，心思獨運，氣韻厚重沈鬱，迥不猶人。

translations.literal: He studied painting under Wang Shimin; his mind worked alone, breath and resonance heavy, thick, and somber, utterly unlike others.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Wang Shimin; his mind worked independently, and his work was dense, weighty, and somber—utterly unlike others.

sentences.zh: 晚年棄家從天主教，曾再遊歐羅巴。

translations.literal: In his late years he abandoned his family and followed Catholicism, and once traveled again to Europe.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he left his family for Catholicism and traveled again to Europe.

sentences.zh: 作畫每用西洋法，雲氣綿渺凌虛，迥異平時。

translations.literal: Whenever he painted he often used Western methods; clouds and mist were hazy and lofty in the void, utterly different from ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: He often employed Western techniques; his clouds and mist rose with airy distance unlike his usual manner.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十七年，卒，年八十七。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi he died, aged eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi, at the age of eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 當時或言其浮海不歸，後於上海南郭得其墓碣，題曰「天學修士」雲。

translations.literal: At the time some said he had sailed the sea and not returned; later at the south wall of Shanghai his tomb stele was found, inscribed "Celestial Learning Cultivator."
translations.idiomatic: Some said he had sailed away and never returned; later his tomb stele was found outside Shanghai's south wall, inscribed Celestial Learning Cultivator.

sentences.zh: 翬初與友善，後絕交。

translations.literal: At first he was friendly with Hui; later they broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: He was once friendly with Hui, but they later broke off contact.

sentences.zh: 王原祁論畫。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanqi's discourse on painting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanqi's remarks on painting:

sentences.zh: 右歷而左翬，曰：「邇時畫手，惟吳漁山而已。」

translations.literal: To the right was Li and to the left Hui; he said: "Among painters of recent times, only Wu Yushan."
translations.idiomatic: With Li to his right and Hui to his left, he said, "Among recent painters, only Wu Yushan."

sentences.zh: 世以時敏、鑑、翬、原祁、歷及惲格，並稱為六大家。

translations.literal: The age together styled Shimin, Jian, Hui, Yuanqi, Li, and Yun Ge the Six Great Masters.
translations.idiomatic: The age grouped Shimin, Jian, Hui, Yuanqi, Li, and Yun Shouping as the Six Great Masters.

sentences.zh: 同縣又有楊晉、黃鼎。

translations.literal: In the same county there were also Yang Jin and Huang Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county were also Yang Jin and Huang Ding.

sentences.zh: 晉，字子鶴。

translations.literal: Jin, styled Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jin, whose style name was Zihe.

sentences.zh: 翬弟子，山水清秀，尤以畫牛名。

translations.literal: A disciple of Hui; his landscapes were clear and beautiful, and he was especially famed for painting oxen.
translations.idiomatic: A pupil of Hui, his landscapes were refined, and he was especially famed for painting cattle.

sentences.zh: 翬作圖，凡有人物與轎駝馬牛羊，皆命晉寫之。

translations.literal: When Hui made pictures, whenever there were figures or sedan chairs, camels, horses, cattle, or sheep, he ordered Jin to paint them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hui's compositions included figures, sedan chairs, camels, horses, cattle, or sheep, he had Jin paint them.

sentences.zh: 從翬繪南巡圖，因摹內府名跡進禦。

translations.literal: Following Hui in painting the Southern Tour picture, he copied famous traces in the inner storehouse and presented them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting Hui on the Southern Tour scroll, he copied masterpieces from the imperial collection and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 鼎，字尊古。

translations.literal: Ding, styled Zungu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ding, whose style name was Zungu.

sentences.zh: 學於王原祁，而私淑翬，得其意。

translations.literal: He studied under Wang Yuanqi but privately admired Hui and obtained his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Wang Yuanqi but privately revered Hui and grasped his spirit.

sentences.zh: 臨摹古人輒逼真，尤擅元王蒙法。

translations.literal: Whenever he copied the ancients he was invariably true to life, especially skilled in the Yuan master Wang Meng's method.
translations.idiomatic: His copies of the ancients were invariably lifelike, especially in the manner of the Yuan master Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 遍遊名山，號獨往客。

translations.literal: He traveled famous mountains everywhere and styled himself the Lone Traveler.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled famous mountains throughout the land and called himself the Lone Traveler.

sentences.zh: 論者謂翬看盡古今名畫，下筆具有淵源；

translations.literal: Critics said Hui had seen all famous paintings through the ages, and when he set brush to paper he had deep sources;
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Hui had seen every great painting of the past and painted with deep roots;

sentences.zh: 鼎看盡九州山水，下筆具有生氣。

translations.literal: Ding had seen all the mountains and waters of the Nine Provinces, and when he set brush to paper he had living breath.
translations.idiomatic: Ding had seen the mountains and rivers of the entire realm, and painted with living vitality.

sentences.zh: 常客宋犖家，梁、宋間其跡獨多。

translations.literal: He often stayed at Song Luo's house; between Liang and Song his traces alone were most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He often stayed with Song Luo; between Liang and Song his works were especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 方士庶，字循遠，號小師道人，安徽歙縣人，家於揚州。

translations.literal: Fang Shidu, styled Xunyuan, sobriquet Little Master Daoist, a man of She County in Anhui, with home in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shidu, whose style name was Xunyuan and sobriquet Little Master Daoist, was from She County in Anhui and lived in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 鼎弟子，早有出藍之目。

translations.literal: A disciple of Ding, from early on he had the reputation of surpassing his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: A pupil of Ding, he was early hailed as surpassing his teacher.

sentences.zh: 年甫逾四十，卒，論者惜之。

translations.literal: He had just passed forty when he died; critics mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He died barely past forty, to the regret of critics.

sentences.zh: 翬畫派為一代所宗，世比之王士禎之詩，當時門弟子甚盛，傳衍其法者益眾，附著其尤者。

translations.literal: Hui's painting school was revered for a generation, compared to Wang Shizhen's poetry; disciples at his gate were very numerous, and those who transmitted his method grew ever more—those especially notable are appended.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's school dominated a generation, as Wang Shizhen dominated poetry; his disciples were legion, and those who carried on his method were even more numerous—the most notable are recorded below.

sentences.zh: 惲格，字壽平，後以字行，改字正叔，​​號南田，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Yun Ge, styled Shouping, later using the style name as his public name, changed style to Zhengshu, sobriquet Nantian, a man of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Shouping, styled Shouping and later known by that name, then changed his style name to Zhengshu and took the sobriquet Nantian; he came from Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父日初，見隱逸傳。

translations.literal: His father Ruchu is treated in the Biographies of Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun Ruchu is recorded in the Biographies of Recluses.

sentences.zh: 格年十三，從父至​​閩。

translations.literal: When Ge was thirteen he followed his father to Min.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Yun followed his father to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時王祈起兵建寧，日初依之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Qi raised troops at Jianning and Ruchu attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qi raised forces at Jianning, Ruchu joined him.

sentences.zh: 總督陳錦兵克建寧，格被掠，錦妻撫以為子。

translations.literal: Governor Chen Jin's troops took Jianning; Ge was carried off, and Jin's wife raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Chen Jin captured Jianning, Yun was taken captive and Jin's wife adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 從遊杭州靈隱寺，日初偵遇之，紿使出家為僧，乃得歸。

translations.literal: Traveling to Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou, Ruchu spied and met him, deceived him into leaving home as a monk, and thus he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou Ruchu found him, had him feign taking monastic vows, and thus brought him home.

sentences.zh: 格以父忠於明，不應舉，擅詩名，鬻畫養父。

translations.literal: Ge, because his father was loyal to the Ming, did not compete in the examinations, was skilled in poetic fame, and sold paintings to support his father.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had remained loyal to the Ming, Yun refused the civil examinations, won fame in poetry, and sold paintings to support him.

sentences.zh: 畫出天性，山水學元王蒙。

translations.literal: Painting came from inborn nature; in landscape he studied the Yuan master Wang Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Painting came naturally to him; in landscape he studied the Yuan master Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 既與王翬交，曰：「君獨步矣！

translations.literal: Having become friends with Wang Hui, he said: "You walk alone!
translations.idiomatic: Once he befriended Wang Hui and said, "You stand alone in landscape!

sentences.zh: 吾不為第二手。」

translations.literal: I will not be a second hand."
translations.idiomatic: I will not be second to anyone."

sentences.zh: 遂兼用徐熙、黃筌法作花鳥，天機物趣，畢集豪端，比之天仙化人。

translations.literal: He then also used Xu Xi and Huang Quan's methods for birds and flowers; natural aptitude and the interest of things all gathered at the brush tip, compared to a celestial immortal transformed among men.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to Xu Xi and Huang Quan's methods for birds and flowers; natural grace and living spirit gathered at his brush, as if a transcendent had descended to earth.

sentences.zh: 畫成，輒自題詠書之，世號「南田三絕」。

translations.literal: Whenever a painting was finished he would compose and inscribe poetry on it; the age styled this the "Three Perfections of Nantian."
translations.idiomatic: When he finished a painting he inscribed it with his own poetry; the age called this the Three Perfections of Nantian.

sentences.zh: 雖自專意寫生，間作山水，皆超逸，得元人冷淡幽雋之致。

translations.literal: Although he devoted himself to sketching from life, occasionally doing landscape, all were transcendent, obtaining the Yuan people's cool, remote, subtle, and refined flavor.
translations.idiomatic: Though he specialized in sketching from life, his occasional landscapes were equally transcendent, with the cool, subtle restraint of Yuan masters.

sentences.zh: 王時敏聞其名，招之，不時至。

translations.literal: Wang Shimin heard his name and summoned him; he did not come at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shimin heard of him and summoned him, but he did not come promptly.

sentences.zh: 至，則時敏已病，榻前一握手而已。

translations.literal: When he came, Shimin was already ill; before the couch only a single handshake.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived Shimin was already ill and could only grasp his hand once at the bedside.

sentences.zh: 家酷貧，風雨常閉門餓，以金幣乞畫者，非其人不與。

translations.literal: His family was desperately poor; in wind and rain he often shut his door hungry; those who begged paintings with gold and coins—if not the right person he would not give.
translations.idiomatic: His household was desperately poor; in foul weather he often went hungry behind closed doors, and he painted only for those he deemed worthy.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年，卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 子不能具喪，王翬葬之。

translations.literal: His son could not provide full funeral rites; Wang Hui buried him.
translations.idiomatic: His son could not afford a proper funeral; Wang Hui buried him.

sentences.zh: 從父向，字道生。

translations.literal: His father's younger brother Xiang, styled Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yun Xiang, whose style name was Daosheng,

sentences.zh: 自明季以畫著，山水得董源法，格少即師之。

translations.literal: From the late Ming was renowned in painting; in landscape he obtained Dong Yuan's method, and Ge in youth took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: had been renowned for painting since the late Ming; his landscapes followed Dong Yuan, and Yun studied under him in youth.

sentences.zh: 及格負重名，群從子弟多工畫。

translations.literal: When Ge bore a heavy reputation, many cousins and nephews were skilled in painting.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yun won great fame, many kinsmen excelled at painting.

sentences.zh: 其著者源濬，字哲長，官天津縣丞。

translations.literal: The most notable was Yuan Jun, styled Zhechang, who served as assistant magistrate of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The most notable was Yuan Jun, styled Zhechang, who served as assistant magistrate of Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 能傳徐熙法，筆有生氣。

translations.literal: Able to transmit Xu Xi's method, his brush had living breath.
translations.idiomatic: He transmitted Xu Xi's manner and painted with living vitality.

sentences.zh: 族曾孫鍾廕之女曰冰，尤有名，詳列女傳。

translations.literal: A clan great-grandniece of Zhongyin named Bing was especially renowned; she is treated in detail in the Biographies of Women.
translations.idiomatic: His clan great-grandniece Zhongyin's daughter Bing was especially celebrated and is recorded in the Biographies of Women.

sentences.zh: 其弟子尤著者：馬元馭，字扶曦，常熟人。

translations.literal: Among his disciples the most renowned: Ma Yuanyu, styled Fuxi, a man of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: His most celebrated pupils included Ma Yuanyu, styled Fuxi, of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 家貧，好讀書。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor, he loved learning.

sentences.zh: 幼即工畫，王翬稱之。

translations.literal: From youth he was skilled at painting, and Wang Hui praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He showed painting talent from childhood, and Wang Hui praised his work.

sentences.zh: 後學於格，得其逸筆，頗稱入室。

translations.literal: Later he studied under Ge and obtained his free brushwork, and was widely said to have entered the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied under Yun Nantian and mastered his free, effortless brushwork, earning a reputation for true mastery.

sentences.zh: 孫女荃，傳其學，名與惲冰相匹。

translations.literal: His granddaughter Quan transmitted his learning, and her fame matched that of Yun Bing.
translations.idiomatic: His granddaughter Sun Quan carried on his art, and her reputation rivaled that of Yun Bing.

sentences.zh: 元馭嘗以畫法授同縣蔣廷錫，後廷錫宮禁近，以書招之，謝不往。

translations.literal: Yuanyu once taught painting methods to Jiang Tingxi of the same county; later, when Tingxi was close to the palace precincts, he summoned him by letter, but Yuanyu declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu once taught painting to his fellow townsman Jiang Tingxi; later, when Tingxi held a post near the palace, he invited Yuanyu by letter, but Yuanyu politely refused.

sentences.zh: 格人品絕高，寫生為一代之冠，私淑者眾，然不能得其機趣神韻。

translations.literal: Ge's character was supremely lofty; in life-drawing he was the crown of his generation, and many privately admired him, yet they could not obtain his spirit, interest, and resonance.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Nantian's character was exceptionally noble, and in life-drawing he stood at the head of his age; many sought to emulate him, yet none could capture his vital spirit and resonance.

sentences.zh: 惟乾隆中華嵒號為繼跡。

translations.literal: Only in the Qianlong era was Hua Yan said to continue his footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the Qianlong reign was Hua Yan regarded as his true successor.

sentences.zh: 後改琦亦差得其意云。

translations.literal: Later Gai Qi also somewhat obtained his intent, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Gai Qi is also said to have come somewhat close to his spirit.

sentences.zh: 王武，字勤中，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Wu, styled Qinzhong, was a man of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wu, styled Qinzhong, was from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 畫花草，流麗多風，王時敏亦稱為妙品，學者宗之。

translations.literal: He painted flowers and grasses with flowing beauty and abundant spirit; Wang Shimin also called them marvelous works, and students took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: His flower-and-grass paintings were graceful and spirited; Wang Shimin also praised them as masterworks, and painters took him as their model.

sentences.zh: 及格出，遂掩其上。

translations.literal: When Ge emerged, he then overshadowed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun Nantian rose to fame, he eclipsed Wang Wu's reputation.

sentences.zh: 沈銓，字南蘋，浙江德清人。

translations.literal: Shen Quan, styled Nanping, was a man of Deqing in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Quan, styled Nanping, was from Deqing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 工寫花鳥，專精設色，妍麗絕人。

translations.literal: He was skilled at painting flowers and birds, specialized in color application, and was surpassingly beautiful among men.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at flower-and-bird painting and specialized in color application, with a beauty that surpassed all others.

sentences.zh: 雍正中，日本國王聘往授畫，三年乃歸，故其國尤重銓畫，於格為別派。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng era the king of Japan invited him to go and teach painting; after three years he returned, so that country especially valued Quan's paintings, forming a separate branch from Ge.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign the Japanese king invited him to teach painting; he returned after three years, and his art became especially prized in Japan as a branch distinct from Yun Nantian's school.

sentences.zh: 龔賢，字半千，江南崑山人。

translations.literal: Gong Xian, styled Banqian, was a man of Kunshan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Xian, styled Banqian, was from Kunshan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 寓江寧，結廬清涼山下，葺半畝園，隱居自得。

translations.literal: He sojourned in Jiangning, built a hut beneath Qingliang Mountain, repaired the Half-Mu Garden, and lived in seclusion contentedly.
translations.idiomatic: He settled in Jiangning, built a cottage below Qingliang Mountain, tended the Half-Mu Garden, and lived in contented retirement.

sentences.zh: 性孤僻，詩文不苟作。

translations.literal: By nature he was solitary and aloof, and did not compose poetry or prose casually.
translations.idiomatic: Solitary by nature, he wrote poetry and prose only when moved to do so.

sentences.zh: 畫得董源法，埽除蹊徑，獨出幽異，自謂前無古人，後無來者。

translations.literal: In painting he obtained Dong Yuan's method, swept away beaten paths, and stood alone in subtle strangeness, declaring himself without predecessor among the ancients and without successor among those to come.
translations.idiomatic: His painting followed Dong Yuan's method yet swept away convention, achieving a singular subtle strangeness; he claimed that no one before or after could match him.

sentences.zh: 同時與樊圻、高岑、鄒喆、吳弘、葉欣、胡造、謝蓀號「金陵八家」。

translations.literal: At the same time, together with Fan Qi, Gao Cen, Zou Zhe, Wu Hong, Ye Xin, Hu Zao, and Xie Sun, he was called the Eight Masters of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He and Fan Qi, Gao Cen, Zou Zhe, Wu Hong, Ye Xin, Hu Zao, and Xie Sun were known as the Eight Masters of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 圻，字會公；

translations.literal: Qi, styled Huigong;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qi, styled Huigong;

sentences.zh: 造，字石公，與蓀，皆江寧人。

translations.literal: Zao, styled Shigong, and Sun were all men of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zao, styled Shigong, and Xie Sun were all from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 岑，字蔚生，杭州人。

translations.literal: Cen, styled Weisheng, was a man of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cen, styled Weisheng, was from Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 喆。

translations.literal: Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhe.

sentences.zh: 字方魯，吳人。

translations.literal: Styled Fanglu, a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Styled Fanglu, he was from Wu.

sentences.zh: 弘，字遠度，金谿人。

translations.literal: Hong, styled Yuandu, was a man of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hong, styled Yuandu, was from Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 欣，字榮木，華亭人。

translations.literal: Xin, styled Rongmu, was a man of Huating.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xin, styled Rongmu, was from Huating.

sentences.zh: 諸家皆擅雅筆，負時譽，要以賢為稱首。

translations.literal: All these schools were skilled in refined brushwork and bore contemporary fame, yet Xian was taken as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: All were masters of refined brushwork and enjoyed contemporary renown, but Gong Xian was regarded as the foremost.

sentences.zh: 清初畫學蔚盛，大江以南，作者尤多，各成派別，以婁東王時敏為大宗。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, painting flourished luxuriantly; south of the great river there were especially many practitioners, each forming separate schools, with Wang Shimin of Loudong as the great lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qing painting flourished, especially south of the Yangzi, where artists formed distinct schools with Wang Shimin of Loudong as the leading master.

sentences.zh: 若金陵、雲間、嘉禾、新安，皆聞人迭起。

translations.literal: Such places as Jinling, Yunjian, Jiahe, and Xin'an all saw renowned figures rise one after another.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinling, Yunjian, Jiahe, and Xin'an, celebrated painters arose in succession.

sentences.zh: 趙左，字文度，華亭人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zuo, styled Wendu, was a man of Huating.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zuo, styled Wendu, was from Huating.

sentences.zh: 畫出於宋旭，為雲間派之首，吳、松間多宗之。

translations.literal: His painting came from Song Xu and was the head of the Yunjian school; many between Wu and Songjiang took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: His painting derived from Song Xu and led the Yunjian school; painters throughout the Wu-Songjiang region followed his example.

sentences.zh: 項聖謨，字孔彰，嘉興人，元汴之孫。

translations.literal: Xiang Shengmo, styled Kongzhang, was a man of Jiaxing and a grandson of Yuan Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Shengmo, styled Kongzhang, was from Jiaxing and a grandson of Yuan Bian.

sentences.zh: 初學文徵明，後益進於古，董其昌稱其與宋人血戰，又得元人氣韻。

translations.literal: At first he studied Wen Zhengming, then advanced further into antiquity; Dong Qichang said he fought in bloody battle with the Song masters yet also obtained the spirit and resonance of the Yuan masters.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied Wen Zhengming, then pushed deeper into antiquity; Dong Qichang praised him for wrestling with the Song masters yet capturing the spirit of the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子奎，字東井，世其學。

translations.literal: His son Kui, styled Dongjing, inherited his learning through generations.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang Kui, styled Dongjing, carried on the family art.

sentences.zh: 同縣李琪枝，字云連，日華之孫。

translations.literal: Li Qizhi of the same county, styled Yunlian, was a grandson of Rihua.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qizhi of the same county, styled Yunlian, was a grandson of Li Rihua.

sentences.zh: 山水淡逸，傳世者梅竹為多。

translations.literal: His landscapes were light and remote; among works handed down, plum and bamboo were most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: His landscapes were spare and elegant; most of his surviving works are plum and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 項、李皆名族，濡染有緒，群從多以畫名。

translations.literal: Xiang and Li were both distinguished clans, steeped in tradition in orderly succession, and many kinsmen were famed for painting.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Xiang and Li families were eminent clans with long artistic traditions, and many kinsmen won fame as painters.

sentences.zh: 其後雍、乾中錢綸光妻陳書，花鳥人物並工，詳列女傳。

translations.literal: Later, in the Yongzheng and Qianlong eras, Qian Lünguang's wife Chen Shu was skilled in both flower-and-bird and figure painting; she is treated in detail in the Biographies of Women.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the Yongzheng and Qianlong reigns, Qian Lünguang's wife Chen Shu excelled at both flower-and-bird and figure painting and is recorded in the Biographies of Women.

sentences.zh: 錢氏子孫及閨秀傳其法者眾，更盛於項、李二家。

translations.literal: Many descendants of the Qian clan and talented women transmitted her methods, flourishing even more than the Xiang and Li families.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the Qian descendants and talented women carried on her methods, and their school flourished even more than those of the Xiang and Li families.

sentences.zh: 張庚，字浦山，亦嘉興人。

translations.literal: Zhang Geng, styled Pushan, was also a man of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Geng, styled Pushan, was also from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 學於書，深通畫理，著畫徵錄及續錄，自明末至乾、嘉中，所載四百馀人。

translations.literal: He studied books, deeply understood painting principles, and wrote the Record of Painting Portents and its sequel, recording more than four hundred persons from the late Ming to the Qianlong and Jiaqing eras.
translations.idiomatic: A learned man deeply versed in painting theory, he wrote the Record of Painting Portents and its sequel, covering more than four hundred artists from the late Ming through the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns.

sentences.zh: 查士標，字二瞻，號梅壑，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: Zha Shibiao, styled Erzhan and known as Meihe, was a man of She County in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zha Shibiao, styled Erzhan and known as Meihe, was from She County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 明諸生，後棄舉子業，專精書畫。

translations.literal: A licentiate of the Ming, he later abandoned the pursuit of examination degrees and devoted himself exclusively to calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: A Ming-era licentiate, he later abandoned the civil service examinations and devoted himself entirely to calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 家饒於貲，多藏鼎彝古器，及宋、元名跡。

translations.literal: His family was rich in wealth and collected many ancient bronzes and vessels, as well as famous works from the Song and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His family was wealthy and collected ancient bronzes and masterpieces from the Song and Yuan dynasties.

sentences.zh: 初學倪瓚，後參以吳鎮、董其昌法，稱逸品。

translations.literal: At first he studied Ni Zan, then blended in the methods of Wu Zhen and Dong Qichang, and was called a transcendent work.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied Ni Zan, then incorporated the methods of Wu Zhen and Dong Qichang, earning praise as a master of transcendent refinement.

sentences.zh: 晚益以幽淡為宗，疏嬾罕接賓客，蓋託以逃世。

translations.literal: In later years he increasingly took subtle plainness as his standard, was lax and lazy and rarely received guests, probably using this to withdraw from the world.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he increasingly favored subtle restraint, kept to himself, and rarely received guests, using solitude to withdraw from the world.

sentences.zh: 與同縣孫逸，休寧汪之瑞、釋弘仁，號「新安四家」。

translations.literal: Together with Sun Yi of the same county, Wang Zhirui of Xiuning, and the monk Hongren, he was called the Four Masters of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Sun Yi of the same county, Wang Zhirui of Xiuning, and the monk Hongren, he was known as one of the Four Masters of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 久寓揚州，康熙三十七年，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: He long sojourned in Yangzhou; in the thirty-seventh year of Kangxi he died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Yangzhou for many years and died there in the thirty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign, at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 逸，字無逸。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yi, styled Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 流寓蕪湖，曾繪歙山二十四圖。

translations.literal: He wandered and sojourned in Wuhu and once painted the Twenty-Four Views of She Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Wuhu for a time and once painted the Twenty-Four Views of She Mountain.

sentences.zh: 之瑞，字無瑞。

translations.literal: Zhirui, styled Wurui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhirui, styled Wurui.

sentences.zh: 豪邁自喜，渴筆焦墨，酒酣揮灑如風雨。

translations.literal: Bold and expansive, he delighted in himself; with thirsty brush and scorched ink, when wine was warm he wielded the brush like wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and self-assured, he painted with dry brush and scorched ink, wielding his brush like wind and rain when warmed by wine.

sentences.zh: 時當塗蕭雲從，字尺木。

translations.literal: At that time there was Xiao Yuncong of Dangtu, styled Chimu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Xiao Yuncong of Dangtu, styled Chimu.

sentences.zh: 與逸齊名，山水不專宗法，兼長人物。

translations.literal: He was equally famous with Yi; in landscape he did not exclusively follow one school, and he was also skilled in figures.
translations.idiomatic: He was as celebrated as Sun Yi; his landscapes did not follow any single school exclusively, and he was also skilled at figure painting.

sentences.zh: 於採石太白樓下四壁畫五嶽圖，又畫太平山水及離騷圖，好事者並鐫刻以傳。

translations.literal: At the Taibai Tower below Caishi he painted the Five Sacred Mountains on four walls, and also painted landscapes of Taiping and illustrations of the Lisao; enthusiasts all had them carved in stone to transmit them.
translations.idiomatic: At the Taibai Tower below Caishi he painted the Five Sacred Mountains on four walls, and also painted landscapes of Taiping and illustrations of the Lisao; enthusiasts had them carved in stone for circulation.

sentences.zh: 高其佩，字韋之，號且園，奉天遼陽人，隸籍漢軍。

translations.literal: Gao Qipei, styled Weizhi and known as Qieyuan, was a man of Liaoyang in Fengtian and registered among the Han Bannermen.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qipei, styled Weizhi and known as Qieyuan, was from Liaoyang in Fengtian and registered among the Han Bannermen.

sentences.zh: 父殉耿籓之難，其佩以廕官至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father died martyred in the disaster of Prince Geng's rebellion; Qipei by inherited privilege rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father died in Prince Geng's rebellion; Qipei inherited office and rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 畫有奇致，人物山水，並蒼渾沉厚，衣紋如草篆，一袖數折。

translations.literal: His painting had a strange refinement; figures and landscapes alike were dark, full, and deep, with robe folds like grass-seal script, several folds in one sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: His painting had a singular power; figures and landscapes alike were dark and substantial, with robe folds like seal script, several creases in a single sleeve.

sentences.zh: 尤善指畫，嘗畫黃初平叱石成羊，或已成羊而起立，或將成而未起，或半成而未離為石，風趣橫生。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at finger painting; once he painted Huang Chuping commanding stones to become sheep—some already sheep and rising to stand, some about to become but not yet risen, some half-formed and not yet leaving their stone state—and charm sprang forth everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at finger painting; in one work on Huang Chuping turning stones into sheep, some sheep had fully formed and risen, some were still transforming, and some remained half stone—each with vivid charm.

sentences.zh: 畫龍、虎，皆極其態。

translations.literal: In painting dragons and tigers, he fully captured their forms.
translations.idiomatic: His dragons and tigers captured their forms to the fullest.

sentences.zh: 世既重其指墨，晚年以便於揮灑，遂不復用筆。

translations.literal: Since the world already prized his finger ink, in his later years, for ease of wielding the brush, he no longer used the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Because the world already prized his finger painting, in his later years he stopped using the brush altogether for the freedom it allowed.

sentences.zh: 其筆劃之佳，幾無人知之。

translations.literal: The excellence of his brushwork was known to almost no one.
translations.idiomatic: Almost no one knew how fine his brushwork could be.

sentences.zh: 雍正十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yongzheng he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of the Yongzheng reign.

sentences.zh: 甥李世倬、硃倫瀚皆學於其佩。

translations.literal: His nephews Li Shizhuo and Zhu Lunhan both studied under Qipei.
translations.idiomatic: His nephews Li Shizhuo and Zhu Lunhan both studied under him.

sentences.zh: 世倬，字漢章，總督如龍子。

translations.literal: Shizhuo, styled Hanzhang, was the son of Governor Rulong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhuo, styled Hanzhang, was the son of Governor Li Rulong.

sentences.zh: 官至右通政。

translations.literal: His office reached Right Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Right Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 少至江南，從王翬遊，得其傳。

translations.literal: In youth he went to Jiangnan, followed Wang Hui in travel, and obtained his transmission.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he traveled to Jiangnan and studied under Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 後官山西，觀吳道子水陸道場圖，悟人物之法。

translations.literal: Later, while serving in Shanxi, he viewed Wu Daozi's Water-Land Ritual Assembly painting and understood the method of figures.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while serving in Shanxi, he studied Wu Daozi's Water-Land Ritual Assembly and grasped the art of figure painting.

sentences.zh: 花鳥寫生，得其佩指墨之趣，易以筆運，各名一家。

translations.literal: In flower-and-bird life-drawing he obtained Qipei's finger-ink interest and transferred it to brush handling; each established a separate school.
translations.idiomatic: In flower-and-bird painting he adapted Qipei's finger-painting spirit to the brush, and each nephew established his own school.

sentences.zh: 倫瀚，字涵齋，明裔也，隸籍漢軍。

translations.literal: Lunhan, styled Hanzhai, was a descendant of the Ming and registered among the Han Bannermen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lunhan, styled Hanzhai, was a Ming descendant registered among the Han Bannermen.

sentences.zh: 官至都統，直內廷。

translations.literal: His office reached Commandant and he served directly in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Commandant and served directly at court.

sentences.zh: 指畫師其佩，丘壑奇而正，色淡味厚。

translations.literal: In finger painting he took Qipei as master; his hills and ravines were strange yet upright, with pale color and rich flavor.
translations.idiomatic: In finger painting he followed Qipei; his landscapes were bold yet balanced, with pale colors and deep resonance.

sentences.zh: 喜作巨障，元氣淋漓。

translations.literal: He liked to make huge screens, with vital energy pouring forth.
translations.idiomatic: He favored large screens, painted with overflowing vitality.

sentences.zh: 指上生有肉錐，故作人物，鬚眉尤有神，出於天授。

translations.literal: Flesh cones grew on his fingers, so when painting figures the beard and eyebrows were especially spirited, a gift from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Calluses formed on his fingertips, and in figure painting his beards and eyebrows were especially vivid—a gift of nature.

sentences.zh: 其後傳其佩法者，有傅雯、瑛寶。

translations.literal: Later those who transmitted Qipei's method included Fu Wen and Ying Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Later practitioners who carried on Qipei's method included Fu Wen and Ying Bao.

sentences.zh: 雯，字凱亭。

translations.literal: Wen, styled Kaiting.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Wen, styled Kaiting.

sentences.zh: 奉天布衣，為諸王邸客，京師多其遺跡。

translations.literal: A commoner of Fengtian, he was a guest in princes' mansions, and the capital has many traces of his work.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner from Fengtian, he served as a guest in princes' households, and many of his works survive in the capital.

sentences.zh: 瑛寶，字夢禪，滿洲人，大學士永貴子。

translations.literal: Ying Bao, styled Mengchan, was a Manchu and the son of Grand Secretary Yonggui.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Bao, styled Mengchan, was a Manchu and the son of Grand Secretary Yonggui.

sentences.zh: 以疾辭廕不仕，詩畫自娛。

translations.literal: Because of illness he declined inherited privilege and did not serve, amusing himself with poetry and painting.
translations.idiomatic: He declined inherited office because of illness and amused himself with poetry and painting.

sentences.zh: 指墨以簡貴勝，深自矜許。

translations.literal: In finger ink he triumphed through simplicity and dignity, and deeply prided himself on it.
translations.idiomatic: His finger painting triumphed through spare elegance, and he took great pride in it.

sentences.zh: 張鵬翀，字天飛，自號南華山人，江蘇嘉定人。

translations.literal: Zhang Pengchong, styled Tianfei and calling himself the Hermit of Nanhua, was a man of Jiading in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pengchong, styled Tianfei and calling himself the Hermit of Nanhua, was from Jiading in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年進士，入翰林，官至詹事府詹事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifth year of Yongzheng, he entered the Hanlin Academy and his office reached Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign, he entered the Hanlin Academy and rose to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 天才超邁，詩畫皆援筆立就，瀟酒自適，類其為人。
