translations.literal: His talent was surpassing; in poetry and painting he took up the brush and finished at once, free and easy in self-content, like his person.
translations.idiomatic: His talent was extraordinary; he could finish poems and paintings at a stroke, with an easy grace that matched his character.

sentences.zh: 高宗愛其才，不次拔擢。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor loved his talent and promoted him out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor admired his talent and promoted him ahead of schedule.

sentences.zh: 進奉詩文，多寓規於頌。

translations.literal: In presenting poetry and prose, he often lodged admonition within praise.
translations.idiomatic: In the poems and essays he presented at court, he often embedded remonstrance within praise.

sentences.zh: 畫無師承，自然入古。

translations.literal: In painting he had no teacher's transmission and naturally entered antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He had no formal painting master yet naturally achieved an antique quality.

sentences.zh: 雖應制之作，蕭散若不經意，愈見神韻。

translations.literal: Even in works made to order, he was sparse and free as if careless, revealing spirit and resonance all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Even in court commissions his work seemed effortless and spare, revealing all the more of his spirit and resonance.

sentences.zh: 繪春林澹靄圖，題詩進上，上賜和，鵬翀即於宮門疊韻陳謝。

translations.literal: He painted Spring Woods in Light Mist, inscribed a poem and presented it upward; the emperor bestowed a matching poem, and Pengchong immediately at the palace gate offered thanks in linked rhyme.
translations.idiomatic: He painted Spring Woods in Light Mist, inscribed a poem, and presented it to the throne; when the emperor replied in verse, Pengchong immediately composed a linked-rhyme thank-you at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 嘗從駕西苑液池，一渡之頃，得詩八首。

translations.literal: Once, following the imperial procession to the Ye Pool in the Western Park, in the time of one crossing he obtained eight poems.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while accompanying the emperor to the Ye Pool in the Western Park, he composed eight poems during a single crossing.

sentences.zh: 屢敕御舟作畫，賜御筆枇杷折枝及松竹雙清圖，又賜雙清閣書額，迭拜筆硯、文綺之賜無算。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he was ordered to paint on the imperial boat; he was granted the emperor's own brush, loquat branch paintings and pine-and-bamboo twin purity pictures, and also granted the calligraphic plaque for the Twin Purity Pavilion, receiving countless successive gifts of brush, inkstone, and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ordered to paint aboard the imperial boat and received the emperor's own brush, paintings of loquat branches and pine-and-bamboo, and the calligraphic plaque for the Twin Purity Pavilion, along with countless gifts of brush, inkstone, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年，乞假歸，卒於途次。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he requested leave to return home and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Qianlong reign he requested leave to return home and died en route.

sentences.zh: 上眷之，久不忘，對群臣輒曰：「張鵬翀可惜！」

translations.literal: The emperor favored him and long did not forget; facing his ministers he would say: "Zhang Pengchong is a pity!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him and long remembered him; before his ministers he would say, "What a loss Zhang Pengchong is!"

sentences.zh: 自康熙至乾隆朝，當國家全盛，文學侍從諸臣，每以藝事上邀宸眷。

translations.literal: From the Kangxi to the Qianlong reigns, when the state was in full prosperity, the literary attendants often invited imperial favor upward through artistic matters.
translations.idiomatic: From the Kangxi through the Qianlong reigns, when the empire was at its height, literary attendants often won imperial favor through their artistic accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 大學士蔣廷錫及​​子溥，董邦達及子誥，尚書錢維城，侍郎鄒一桂，與鵬翀為尤著。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Jiang Tingxi and his son Pu, Dong Bangda and his son Gao, Minister Qian Weicheng, Vice Minister Zou Yigui, and Pengchong were especially renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Jiang Tingxi and his son Pu, Dong Bangda and his son Gao, Minister Qian Weicheng, Vice Minister Zou Yigui, and Pengchong were especially notable.

sentences.zh: 廷錫以逸筆寫生，奇正、工率、濃淡，一幅間恆間出，無不超脫。

translations.literal: Tingxi used a free brush in life-drawing; the strange and the orthodox, the meticulous and the rough, the dense and the light constantly appeared within a single scroll, all surpassingly free.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxi painted from life with a free brush; within a single scroll the bold and the orthodox, the meticulous and the rough, the dense and the light constantly appeared, all with surpassing freedom.

sentences.zh: 源出於惲格，而不為所囿。

translations.literal: His source came from Yun Ge, yet he was not confined by it.
translations.idiomatic: His art derived from Yun Nantian yet was not bound by it.

sentences.zh: 邦達山水源於董源、巨然、黃公望，墨法得力於董其昌，自王原祁後推為大家。

translations.literal: Bangda's landscape derived from Dong Yuan, Juran, and Huang Gongwang; his ink method drew strength from Dong Qichang, and after Wang Yuanqi he was acclaimed as a great master.
translations.idiomatic: Bangda's landscapes derived from Dong Yuan, Juran, and Huang Gongwang; his ink technique drew on Dong Qichang, and after Wang Yuanqi he was acclaimed as a great master.

sentences.zh: 久直內廷，進御之作，大幅尋丈，小冊寸許，不下數百。

translations.literal: Long serving directly in the inner court, in works presented to the emperor, large scrolls measured in zhang, small albums only inches, numbering no less than several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Serving long at court, he presented hundreds of works to the emperor, from large scrolls several feet across to small albums only inches wide.

sentences.zh: 溥、誥各承其家法。

translations.literal: Pu and Gao each inherited their family's methods.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and Gao each inherited their fathers' methods.

sentences.zh: 維城山水蒼秀，花卉傅色尤有神采。

translations.literal: Weicheng's landscapes were dark and elegant; in flowers his color application especially had spirit and brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng's landscapes were dark and elegant, and his flower paintings were especially vivid in color.

sentences.zh: 一桂以百花卷被宸賞，世謂惲格後罕匹者。

translations.literal: Yigui's Hundred Flowers scroll won imperial praise, and the world said that after Yun Ge there were few to match him.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui's Hundred Flowers scroll won imperial praise, and he was regarded as one of the few painters since Yun Nantian who could match him.

sentences.zh: 諸人所繪併入石渠寶笈，御題褒美，傳為盛事。

translations.literal: The works painted by these men were all entered into the Shiqu Baoji, with imperial inscriptions of praise, transmitted as a grand occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Their paintings were all catalogued in the Shiqu Baoji with imperial inscriptions of praise, and the episode became celebrated.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，尚書黃鉞由主事改官翰林，入直，畫為仁宗所賞。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing era, Minister Huang Yue was transferred from section chief to the Hanlin Academy, entered direct service, and his painting was appreciated by Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign, Minister Huang Yue was transferred from section chief to the Hanlin Academy and entered court service; his painting won the favor of the Jiaqing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 道、咸以後，侍郎戴熙、大學士張之萬，並官禁近，以畫名。

translations.literal: After the Daoguang and Xianfeng eras, Vice Minister Dai Xi and Grand Secretary Zhang Zhiwan both held posts near the palace precincts and were famed for painting.
translations.idiomatic: After the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns, Vice Minister Dai Xi and Grand Secretary Zhang Zhiwan both held posts close to the throne and were famed for their painting.

sentences.zh: 然國家浸以多故，視承平故事稍異焉。

translations.literal: Yet the state gradually had many troubles, and compared with the customs of peaceful times it was somewhat different.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as the empire faced growing troubles, court patronage of the arts differed somewhat from the customs of more peaceful times.

sentences.zh: 唐岱，字毓東，滿洲人。

translations.literal: Tang Dai, styled Yudong, was a Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Dai, styled Yudong, was a Manchu.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，以廕官參領。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era he held the office of assistant commandant by inherited privilege.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he held the post of assistant commandant by inherited privilege.

sentences.zh: 從王原祁學畫，丘壑似原祁。

translations.literal: He studied painting under Wang Yuanqi, and his hills and ravines resembled Yuanqi's.
translations.idiomatic: He studied painting under Wang Yuanqi, and his landscapes closely resembled his master's.

sentences.zh: 供奉內廷，聖祖品題當時以為第一手，稱「畫狀元」。

translations.literal: Serving in the inner court, the sage ancestor's appraisal at the time took him as the foremost hand, and he was called the Painting Jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Serving at court, he was judged by the Kangxi Emperor to be the finest painter of his day and was called the Painting Jinshi.

sentences.zh: 歷事世宗、高宗。

translations.literal: He served through the reigns of Shizong and Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: He served through the reigns of the Yongzheng and Qianlong emperors.

sentences.zh: 高宗在潛邸，即喜其畫，數有題詠，後益被寵遇。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was in the Hidden Residence he already delighted in his painting and repeatedly inscribed poems; later he was increasingly favored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor was still heir apparent he already admired Tang Dai's painting and often inscribed poems on his work; later he received even greater favor.

sentences.zh: 唐岱專工山水，以宋人為宗。

translations.literal: Tang Dai specialized in landscape and took the Song masters as his standard.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Dai specialized in landscape painting and took the Song masters as his model.

sentences.zh: 少時名動公卿。

translations.literal: In youth his fame moved nobles and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth his fame reached the highest circles of court.

sentences.zh: 直內廷久，筆法益進，人間傳播者轉稀。

translations.literal: Serving directly in the inner court for long, his brush method advanced further, yet works circulating among the people became increasingly rare.
translations.idiomatic: After long service at court his brushwork grew ever finer, yet fewer of his works circulated outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 著繪事發微行世。

translations.literal: He wrote Subtle Points in Painting Matters, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Subtle Points in Painting Matters, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 清製，畫史供御者無官秩，設如意館於啟祥宮南，凡繪工、文史及雕琢玉器、裝潢帖軸皆在焉。

translations.literal: Under Qing institutions, painters who served the emperor had no official rank; the Ruyi Studio was established south of the Qixiang Palace, and there were gathered painters, literary men, jade carvers, and mounters of scrolls and albums.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qing practice, court painters held no official rank; the Ruyi Studio was established south of the Qixiang Palace to house painters, scholars, jade carvers, and scroll mounters.

sentences.zh: 初類工匠，後漸用士流，由大臣引薦，或獻畫稱旨召入，與詞臣供奉體制不同。

translations.literal: At first they were like artisans; later men of the literati class were gradually employed, recommended by great ministers or summoned after presenting paintings that pleased the emperor—a system different from that of literary attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At first they were treated like artisans; later literati were gradually employed, recommended by ministers or summoned after presenting paintings that pleased the emperor—a system distinct from that of literary attendants.

sentences.zh: 間賜出身官秩，皆出特賞。

translations.literal: Occasionally they were granted initial official rank, all as special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally they were granted official rank, always as special imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 高宗萬幾之暇，嘗幸館中，每親指授，時以為榮。

translations.literal: In the intervals of Gaozong's myriad affairs, he would visit the studio and personally instruct them; at the time this was regarded as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: In moments free from state affairs, the Qianlong Emperor would visit the studio and personally instruct the painters, an honor greatly prized at the time.

sentences.zh: 其畫之精美者，一體編入石渠寶笈、秘殿珠林二書。

translations.literal: Their finest paintings were all catalogued together in the Shiqu Baoji and the Secret Hall Pearl Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Their finest paintings were all catalogued in the Shiqu Baoji and the Secret Hall Pearl Forest.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，編修胡敬撰國朝院畫錄，凡載八十馀人，其尤卓著可傳者十馀人。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing era Compiler Hu Jing wrote the Record of Court Painting of Our Dynasty, recording more than eighty persons in all, of whom more than ten were especially outstanding and worth transmitting.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign Compiler Hu Jing wrote the Record of Court Painting of Our Dynasty, recording more than eighty artists, of whom more than ten were truly outstanding.

sentences.zh: 焦秉貞，山東濟寧人。

translations.literal: Jiao Bingzhen was a man of Jining in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Bingzhen was from Jining in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，官欽天監五官正。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era he served as Director of the Five Offices in the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he served as Director of the Five Offices in the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 工人物樓觀，通測算，參用西洋畫法，剖析分刌，量度陰陽向背，分別明暗，遠視之，人畜、花木、屋宇皆植立而形圓。

translations.literal: He was skilled at figures and pavilions, understood surveying and calculation, and blended in Western painting methods, analyzing and dividing forms, measuring yin and yang, facing and backing, distinguishing light and dark; viewed from afar, people, livestock, flowers, trees, and buildings all stood upright with rounded forms.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at figures and architecture, understood surveying and calculation, and incorporated Western painting methods, analyzing forms, measuring light and shadow, and distinguishing brightness and shade; viewed from a distance, people, animals, flowers, trees, and buildings all stood upright with rounded forms.

sentences.zh: 聖祖嘉之，命繪耕織圖四十六幅，鐫版印賜臣工。

translations.literal: The sage ancestor praised him and ordered him to paint forty-six pictures of plowing and weaving, which were carved in blocks and printed as gifts for officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor praised him and ordered him to paint forty-six scenes of plowing and weaving, which were carved in woodblocks and printed as gifts for officials.

sentences.zh: 自秉貞創法，畫院多相沿襲。

translations.literal: From the time Bingzhen created his method, the painting academy largely followed and inherited it.
translations.idiomatic: After Bingzhen established his method, the court painting academy largely followed it.

sentences.zh: 其弟子冷枚，膠州人，為最肖。

translations.literal: His disciple Leng Mei, a man of Jiaozhou, was the most faithful likeness.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Leng Mei of Jiaozhou most closely resembled him.

sentences.zh: 與繪萬壽盛典圖。

translations.literal: He also painted the Illustrations of the Grand Celebration of Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped paint the Illustrations of the Grand Celebration of Longevity.

sentences.zh: 陳枚，江蘇婁縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Mei was a man of Lou County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mei was from Lou County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 官內務府郎中。

translations.literal: He served as Director in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 初法宋人，折衷唐寅，後亦參西洋法。

translations.literal: At first he followed the Song masters, reconciled Tang Yin, and later also blended in Western methods.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed the Song masters, then blended in Tang Yin's manner, and later incorporated Western methods as well.

sentences.zh: 寸紙尺縑，圖群山萬壑，人物胥備。

translations.literal: On paper an inch wide or silk a foot long, he depicted myriad mountains and ravines, with figures all complete.
translations.idiomatic: On the smallest sheet he could depict mountains and ravines in full, with every figure in place.

sentences.zh: 郎世寧，西洋人。

translations.literal: Lang Shining was a Westerner.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Shining was a European.

sentences.zh: 康熙中入直，高宗尤賞異。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era he entered direct service, and Gaozong especially admired and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service during the Kangxi reign, and the Qianlong Emperor especially admired him.

sentences.zh: 凡名馬、珍禽、琪花、異草，輒命圖之，無不奕奕如生。

translations.literal: Whenever there were famous horses, rare birds, precious flowers, or exotic plants, he was ordered to depict them, and none failed to appear vivid as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there were famous horses, rare birds, precious flowers, or exotic plants, he was ordered to paint them, and all appeared vividly alive.

sentences.zh: 設色奇麗，非秉貞等所及。

translations.literal: His color application was marvelously beautiful, beyond what Bingzhen and others could reach.
translations.idiomatic: His use of color was marvelously rich, surpassing even Bingzhen and his followers.

sentences.zh: 艾啟蒙，亦西洋人。

translations.literal: Ai Qimeng was also a Westerner.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Qimeng was also a European.

sentences.zh: 其藝亞於郎世寧。

translations.literal: His art was second to Lang Shining.
translations.idiomatic: His art ranked below that of Lang Shining.

sentences.zh: 張宗蒼，字默存，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongcang, styled Mocun, was a man of Wu County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongcang, styled Mocun, was from Wu County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 學畫於黃鼎。

translations.literal: He studied painting under Huang Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He studied painting under Huang Ding.

sentences.zh: 初官河工主簿。

translations.literal: At first he served as Clerk of River Works.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Clerk of River Works.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十六年南巡，獻冊，受特知，召入直。

translations.literal: On the southern tour in the sixteenth year of Qianlong he presented an album, received special recognition, and was summoned to direct service.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern tour of the sixteenth year of the Qianlong reign he presented an album, won special recognition, and was summoned to court service.

sentences.zh: 數年，授戶部主事，以老乞歸。

translations.literal: After several years he was appointed Section Chief in the Ministry of Revenue, then requested retirement because of age.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was appointed Section Chief in the Ministry of Revenue, then retired because of age.

sentences.zh: 宗蒼山水，氣體深厚，多以皴擦取韻，一洗畫院甜熟之習，被恩遇特厚。

translations.literal: Zongcang's landscapes had deep and substantial atmosphere, mostly obtaining resonance through texture strokes and rubbing, washing away the sweet, overripe habits of the painting academy, and he received especially thick favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zongcang's landscapes were deep and substantial, relying largely on texture strokes for their resonance and breaking free of the overly sweet manner of the court academy; he received exceptional imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 所畫著錄石渠者，百十有六，多荷御題。

translations.literal: The works he painted recorded in the Shiqu numbered one hundred sixteen, most bearing imperial inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred sixteen of his paintings were catalogued in the Shiqu Baoji, most bearing imperial inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 弟子徐揚、方琮最得其法，亦邀宸賞，賜揚舉人，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: His disciples Xu Yang and Fang Cong most obtained his method, also won imperial appreciation, and Yang was granted the rank of juren and appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Xu Yang and Fang Cong mastered his method best and also won imperial favor; Yang was granted the rank of juren and appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 余省，字曾三，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Yu Sheng, styled Zengsan, was a man of Changshu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Sheng, styled Zengsan, was from Changshu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 善寫生，能得花外之趣。

translations.literal: He was skilled at life-drawing and could obtain the interest beyond the flowers themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at painting from life and captured the spirit beyond the flowers themselves.

sentences.zh: 同時楊大章，亦賦色修潔，可與鄒一桂頡頏，花鳥以二人為最工。

translations.literal: At the same time Yang Dazhang also applied color with refined elegance, able to match Zou Yigui; in flower-and-bird painting these two men were the most skilled.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Yang Dazhang also applied color with refined elegance and could match Zou Yigui; in flower-and-bird painting these two were the finest.

sentences.zh: 金廷標，字士揆，浙江桐鄉人。

translations.literal: Jin Tingbiao, styled Shikui, was a man of Tongxiang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Tingbiao, styled Shikui, was from Tongxiang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 南巡進白描羅漢，稱旨，召入祇候。

translations.literal: On the southern tour he presented ink-outline arhats, pleased the emperor, and was summoned to attend in waiting.
translations.idiomatic: During a southern tour he presented ink-outline arhat paintings that pleased the emperor, and he was summoned to court service.

sentences.zh: 廷標畫不尚工緻，以機趣傳神。

translations.literal: Tingbiao's painting did not value meticulous refinement but transmitted spirit through vital interest.
translations.idiomatic: Tingbiao did not pursue meticulous refinement but conveyed spirit through vivid interest.

sentences.zh: 高宗題所作琵琶行圖曰：「唐寅舊圖，有琵琶伎在別船，廷標祇繪白居易一人側耳而聽，別有會心。

translations.literal: Gaozong inscribed on his Pipa Song painting: "In Tang Yin's old picture there was a pipa player on a separate boat; Tingbiao painted only Bai Juyi alone listening with inclined ear—a separate kind of understanding.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor inscribed on his Pipa Song painting: "In Tang Yin's old picture the pipa player sits on a separate boat; Tingbiao painted only Bai Juyi listening with inclined ear—a different kind of insight.

sentences.zh: 古人畫意為先，非畫院中人所及。」

translations.literal: The ancients put pictorial idea first, something not reachable by men of the painting academy."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients put pictorial idea first—something beyond the reach of ordinary court painters."

sentences.zh: 會愛烏罕進四駿，郎世寧繪之，復命廷標別作，仿李公麟法，增寫執靮人，古趣出彼上。

translations.literal: When the Khan of Ili presented four fine steeds, Lang Shining painted them, and Tingbiao was again ordered to make a separate version, following Li Gonglin's method and adding grooms holding the reins; its antique interest surpassed the other.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khan of Ili presented four fine steeds, Lang Shining painted them, and Tingbiao was ordered to make a separate version in Li Gonglin's manner, adding grooms holding the reins; its antique spirit surpassed the other.

sentences.zh: 及廷標卒，上命舊黏殿壁者悉付裝池，收入石渠寶笈。

translations.literal: When Tingbiao died, the emperor ordered all his old works pasted on palace walls to be remounted and entered into the Shiqu Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingbiao died, the emperor ordered all his works still pasted on palace walls to be remounted and catalogued in the Shiqu Baoji.

sentences.zh: 丁觀鵬，工人物，效明丁雲鵬，以宋人為法，不尚奇詭。

translations.literal: Ding Guanpeng was skilled at figures, emulated the Ming Ding Yunpeng, took the Song masters as his standard, and did not value the strange and bizarre.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Guanpeng excelled at figure painting, emulated the Ming master Ding Yunpeng, followed the Song masters, and avoided the bizarre.

sentences.zh: 畫仙佛神像最擅長，著錄獨多。

translations.literal: In painting immortals, buddhas, and divine images he was most adept, and his catalogued works alone were most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He was most adept at painting immortals, buddhas, and divine images, and more of his works were catalogued than those of any other.

sentences.zh: 時有嚴弘滋者，南巡兩次獻畫，所作三官神像，秀發飛揚，稱為絕作，屢命畫院諸人摹之。

translations.literal: At the time there was Yan Hongzi, who twice presented paintings on the southern tour; his Three Officials divine images were elegant and soaring, called supreme works, and the academy painters were repeatedly ordered to copy them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Yan Hongzi, who twice presented paintings during southern tours; his Three Officials divine images were elegant and soaring, hailed as supreme works, and court painters were repeatedly ordered to copy them.

sentences.zh: 姚文瀚，亦以人物仙佛名，亞於觀鵬。

translations.literal: Yao Wenhan was also famed for figures, immortals, and buddhas, second to Guanpeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Wenhan was also famed for figures, immortals, and buddhas, ranking below Guanpeng.

sentences.zh: 繆炳泰，字象賓，江蘇江陰人。

translations.literal: Miao Bingtai, styled Xiangbin, was a man of Jiangyin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Bingtai, styled Xiangbin, was from Jiangyin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 初以國子監生召繪御容。

translations.literal: At first, as a student of the Imperial Academy, he was summoned to paint the imperial portrait.
translations.idiomatic: He was first summoned from the Imperial Academy to paint the imperial portrait.

sentences.zh: 南巡，應召試，賜舉人，授中書，官至兵部郎中。

translations.literal: On the southern tour he answered a summons to examination, was granted juren, appointed Secretariat Drafter, and his office reached Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: During a southern tour he answered an imperial summons, was granted the rank of juren, appointed Secretariat Drafter, and rose to Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十年以後御容，皆出所繪。

translations.literal: Imperial portraits after the fiftieth year of Qianlong all came from his brush.
translations.idiomatic: All imperial portraits after the fiftieth year of the Qianlong reign were painted by him.

sentences.zh: 又命繪紫光閣功臣像，人人逼肖，寫真之最工者。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to paint the portraits of meritorious officials at the Ziguang Pavilion; each figure was lifelike, and he was the most skilled in portraiture.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to paint the portraits of meritorious officials at the Ziguang Pavilion; each figure was lifelike, and he was the finest portraitist of his day.

sentences.zh: 畫院盛於康、乾兩朝，以唐岱、郎世寧、張宗蒼、金廷標、丁觀鵬為最，宗蒼所作，尤有士氣，道光以後無聞焉。

translations.literal: The painting academy flourished in the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns, with Tang Dai, Lang Shining, Zhang Zongcang, Jin Tingbiao, and Ding Guanpeng as the foremost; Zongcang's works especially had literati spirit, and after Daoguang there was no further renown.
translations.idiomatic: The court painting academy flourished under the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors, with Tang Dai, Lang Shining, Zhang Zongcang, Jin Tingbiao, and Ding Guanpeng as its greatest masters; Zongcang's work especially had literati spirit, and after the Daoguang reign the academy fell silent.

sentences.zh: 至光緒中，孝欽皇后喜藝事，稍復如意館舊規，畫史皆凡材，無可紀者。

translations.literal: By the Guangxu era Empress Dowager Cixi delighted in artistic matters and slightly restored the old regulations of the Ruyi Studio, but the painters were all mediocre talents, with none worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: By the Guangxu reign Empress Dowager Cixi revived something of the old Ruyi Studio practice, but its painters were mediocre and none worth recording.

sentences.zh: 華嵒，字秋岳，號新羅山人，福建臨汀人。

translations.literal: Hua Yan, styled Qiuyue and known as the Hermit of Xinluo, was a man of Linting in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yan, styled Qiuyue and known as the Hermit of Xinluo, was from Linting in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 慕杭州西湖之勝，家焉。

translations.literal: He admired the beauty of West Lake in Hangzhou and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn to the beauty of West Lake in Hangzhou, he made his home there.

sentences.zh: 畫山水、人物、花鳥、草蟲無不工，脫去時蹊，力追古法。

translations.literal: In landscape, figures, flowers and birds, and grasses and insects there was nothing he did not master; he cast off contemporary paths and strove forcefully after antique methods.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered landscape, figure, flower-and-bird, and insect painting alike, cast off contemporary conventions, and strove to recover antique methods.

sentences.zh: 有時過求超脫，然其率略處，愈不可及。

translations.literal: Sometimes he pursued excessive freedom, yet in his rough and spare places he became all the more unreachable.
translations.idiomatic: At times he pursued excessive freedom, yet in his most spare passages he became all the more inimitable.

sentences.zh: 工詩，有離垢集，古質清峭。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry and had the Collection Free of Stain, ancient in substance and clear and austere.
translations.idiomatic: He was also a fine poet; his Collection Free of Stain is ancient in tone and clear and austere.

sentences.zh: 書法脫俗，世稱「三絕」，可繼惲格。

translations.literal: His calligraphy was free of vulgarity, and the world called him the Three Perfections, able to succeed Yun Ge.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy was free of vulgarity, and the world hailed his Three Perfections as worthy to succeed Yun Nantian.

sentences.zh: 僑居揚州最久，晚歸杭州，卒年近八十。

translations.literal: He sojourned longest in Yangzhou, returned to Hangzhou in his later years, and died near the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He lived longest in Yangzhou, returned to Hangzhou in his later years, and died near the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 乾、嘉之間，浙西畫學稱盛，而揚州遊士所聚，一時名流競逐。

translations.literal: Between the Qianlong and Jiaqing eras painting in western Zhejiang was said to flourish, while Yangzhou gathered wandering scholars and for a time celebrated figures vied in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns painting flourished in western Zhejiang, while Yangzhou drew wandering scholars and celebrated figures in pursuit of art.

sentences.zh: 其尤著者，為高鳳翰、鄭燮、金農、羅聘、奚岡、黃易、錢杜、方薰等。

translations.literal: The most renowned among them were Gao Fenghan, Zheng Xie, Jin Nong, Luo Pin, Xi Gang, Huang Yi, Qian Du, Fang Xun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The most celebrated among them were Gao Fenghan, Zheng Xie, Jin Nong, Luo Pin, Xi Gang, Huang Yi, Qian Du, Fang Xun, and others.

sentences.zh: 鳳翰，字西園，山東膠州人。

translations.literal: Fenghan, styled Xiyuan, was a man of Jiaozhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Fenghan, styled Xiyuan, was from Jiaozhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，以薦得官，署安徽績溪知縣，被劾罷。

translations.literal: In early Yongzheng, through recommendation he obtained office and served as acting magistrate of Jixi in Anhui, but was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yongzheng he obtained office through recommendation and served as acting magistrate of Jixi in Anhui, but was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久寓江、淮間，病偏痺，遂以左手作書畫，縱逸有奇氣。

translations.literal: He long sojourned between the Yangzi and Huai rivers; afflicted with hemiplegia, he then used his left hand for calligraphy and painting, free and expansive with a strange spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He lived for many years between the Yangzi and Huai rivers; stricken with hemiplegia, he took up calligraphy and painting with his left hand, producing work free and expansive with a singular spirit.

sentences.zh: 嘗登焦山觀瘞鶴銘，尋宋陸游題名，親埽積蘚，燃燭捫圖，以敗筆清墨為圖，傳為傑作。

translations.literal: Once he climbed Mount Jiao to view the Buried Crane Inscription, sought out the Song poet Lu You's signature, personally swept away accumulated moss, lit a candle and felt the carving, and made a picture with a worn brush and light ink, transmitted as a masterpiece.
translations.idiomatic: Once he climbed Mount Jiao to view the Buried Crane Inscription, found the Song poet Lu You's signature, swept away the moss himself, lit a candle to trace the carving, and painted the scene with a worn brush and light ink—a work hailed as a masterpiece.

sentences.zh: 性豪邁不羈，藏硯千，手自鐫銘，著硯史。

translations.literal: By nature bold and unrestrained, he collected a thousand inkstones, personally carved inscriptions on them, and wrote the History of Inkstones.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and unrestrained by nature, he collected a thousand inkstones, carved inscriptions on them himself, and wrote the History of Inkstones.

sentences.zh: 又藏司馬相如玉印，秘為至寶。

translations.literal: He also collected Sima Xiangru's jade seal and kept it secret as a supreme treasure.
translations.idiomatic: He also owned a jade seal said to have belonged to Sima Xiangru and treasured it as his greatest possession.

sentences.zh: 盧見曾為兩淮運使，欲觀之，長跪謝不可，其癖類此。

translations.literal: Lu Jianceng, as Transport Commissioner of the Two Huai, wished to view it; Fenghan knelt and declined, unable to grant the request—his obsessions were like this.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Jianceng, Transport Commissioner of the Two Huai, asked to see it, Fenghan knelt and refused—such were his obsessions.

sentences.zh: 燮，字板橋，江蘇興化人。

translations.literal: Xie, styled Banqiao, was a man of Xinghua in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xie, styled Banqiao, was from Xinghua in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年進士，官山東濰縣知縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the first year of Qianlong, he served as magistrate of Weixian in Shandong and had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the first year of the Qianlong reign, he served as magistrate of Weixian in Shandong with a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 辭官鬻畫，作蘭竹，以草書中豎長撇法為蘭葉，書雜分隸法，自號「六分半書」。

translations.literal: He resigned office and sold paintings, making orchids and bamboo; he used the cursive method of vertical long sweeps for orchid leaves, mixed clerical and seal scripts in writing, and called himself the Six-and-a-Half-Part Script.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned from office and sold paintings of orchids and bamboo, using cursive vertical sweeps for orchid leaves and mixing clerical and seal scripts in his writing, which he called the Six-and-a-Half-Part Script.

sentences.zh: 詩詞皆別調，而有摯語。

translations.literal: His poetry and lyrics were all in a separate key, yet had sincere words.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and lyrics were distinctive in tone yet deeply sincere.

sentences.zh: 慷慨嘯傲，慕明徐渭之為人。

translations.literal: Generous and proud, singing freely, he admired the person of the Ming Xu Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Generous and proud, he admired the Ming painter Xu Wei and sought to live as he had.

sentences.zh: 燮同縣李鱓，字復堂。

translations.literal: Xie's fellow townsman Li Shan, styled Futang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xie's fellow townsman Li Shan, styled Futang.

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: A juren.
translations.idiomatic: He was a juren.

sentences.zh: 官山東滕縣知縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Teng County in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Teng County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 花鳥學林良，多得天趣。

translations.literal: In flower-and-bird painting he studied Lin Liang and mostly obtained heaven's interest.
translations.idiomatic: In flower-and-bird painting he studied Lin Liang and captured much of nature's spontaneous charm.

sentences.zh: 陳撰，字楞山，浙江鄞縣人，亦居揚州。

translations.literal: Chen Zhuan, styled Lengshan, was a man of Yin County in Zhejiang and also lived in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhuan, styled Lengshan, was from Yin County in Zhejiang and also lived in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉鴻博，不就試。

translations.literal: Recommended for the Boxue Examination, he did not attend the test.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for the Boxue Hongci examination, he declined to take the test.

sentences.zh: 與鱓齊名，寫梅尤雋逸。

translations.literal: Equally famous with Shan, in painting plum he was especially elegant and free.
translations.idiomatic: He was as celebrated as Li Shan, and his plum paintings were especially elegant and free.

sentences.zh: 農，字壽門，號冬心，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Nong, styled Shoumen and known as Dongxin, was a man of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Nong, styled Shoumen and known as Dongxin, was from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 布衣，薦鴻博，好學癖古，儲金石千卷。

translations.literal: A commoner, recommended for the Boxue Examination, he loved learning and was obsessed with antiquity, storing a thousand scrolls of epigraphy.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner recommended for the Boxue Hongci examination, he loved learning and antiquity and amassed a thousand scrolls of epigraphic records.

sentences.zh: 中歲，遊跡半海內，寄居揚州，遂不歸。

translations.literal: In midlife his travels covered half the empire; he lodged in Yangzhou and never returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In midlife he traveled across much of the empire, settled in Yangzhou, and never returned home.

sentences.zh: 分隸小變漢法，又師禪國山及天發讖兩碑。

translations.literal: In clerical script he slightly altered Han methods and also took as masters the Chan Guoshan and Tianfa Chan steles.
translations.idiomatic: In clerical script he slightly altered Han methods and also studied the Chan Guoshan and Tianfa Chan steles.

sentences.zh: 截毫端，作擘窠大字。

translations.literal: He cut off the tip of the brush and made large characters filling the frame.
translations.idiomatic: He cut the brush tip short and wrote large characters filling the frame.

sentences.zh: 年五十，始從事於畫。

translations.literal: At the age of fifty he first took up painting.
translations.idiomatic: He did not begin painting until the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 初寫竹，師石室老人，號稽留山民。

translations.literal: At first he painted bamboo, taking the Stone Chamber Old Man as master and calling himself the Mountain Man of Jiliu.
translations.idiomatic: He first painted bamboo, claiming the Stone Chamber Old Man as his master and styling himself the Mountain Man of Jiliu.

sentences.zh: 繼畫梅，師白玉蟾，號昔耶居士。

translations.literal: He then painted plum, taking Bai Yuchan as master and calling himself the Layman of Xiye.
translations.idiomatic: He then painted plum, claiming Bai Yuchan as his master and styling himself the Layman of Xiye.

sentences.zh: 又畫馬，自謂得曹、韓法。

translations.literal: He also painted horses and declared that he had obtained the methods of Cao Ba and Han Gan.
translations.idiomatic: He also painted horses and claimed to have mastered the methods of Cao Ba and Han Gan.

sentences.zh: 复畫佛，號心出家盦粥飯僧。

translations.literal: Again he painted buddhas and called himself the Porridge Monk of the Hermitage of the Heart That Has Left Home.
translations.idiomatic: He also painted buddhas and styled himself the Porridge Monk of the Hermitage of the Heart That Has Left Home.

sentences.zh: 其點綴花木，奇柯異葉，皆意為之。

translations.literal: The flowers and trees he added as embellishment, with strange branches and unusual leaves, were all created from imagination.
translations.idiomatic: The flowers and trees with which he embellished his works, with their strange branches and unusual leaves, were all products of imagination.

sentences.zh: 問之，則曰：「貝多龍窠之類也。」

translations.literal: When asked, he would say: "They are like the pipal trees in the Dragon Nest."
translations.idiomatic: When asked, he would say, "They are like the pipal trees in the Dragon Nest."

sentences.zh: 性逋峭，世以迂怪目之。

translations.literal: By nature he was aloof and austere, and the world regarded him as eccentric and strange.
translations.idiomatic: Aloof and austere by nature, he was regarded by the world as eccentric and strange.

sentences.zh: 詩亦鑱削苦硬。

translations.literal: His poetry too was chiseled, austere, and hard.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry too was chiseled, austere, and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 無子，晚手錄以付其女。

translations.literal: He had no son, and in his later years copied out his works by hand and entrusted them to his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son and in his later years copied out his writings by hand for his daughter.

sentences.zh: 歿後，羅聘搜輯雜文編為​​集。

translations.literal: After his death Luo Pin gathered and edited his miscellaneous writings into a collection.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Luo Pin gathered his miscellaneous writings into a collection.

sentences.zh: 聘，字兩峰，江都人。

translations.literal: Pin, styled Liangfeng, was a man of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Pin, styled Liangfeng, was from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 淹雅工詩，從農遊，稱高足弟子，畫無不工。

translations.literal: Refined and elegant, skilled at poetry, he followed Nong in travel and was called a foremost disciple; in painting there was nothing he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and elegant, he was skilled at poetry, studied under Jin Nong, and was hailed as his foremost disciple; he mastered every genre of painting.

sentences.zh: 躭禪悅，夢入招提曰花之寺，彷彿前身，自號花之寺僧。

translations.literal: He delighted in Chan, dreamed he entered a monastery called the Temple of Flowers, as if recalling a previous life, and called himself the Monk of the Temple of Flowers.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to Chan, he dreamed he entered a monastery called the Temple of Flowers, as if recalling a former life, and styled himself the Monk of the Temple of Flowers.

sentences.zh: 多摹佛像，又畫鬼趣圖，​​不一本。

translations.literal: He often copied buddha images and also painted Ghost Scenes, no two alike.
translations.idiomatic: He often copied buddha images and also painted Ghost Scenes, no two versions alike.

sentences.zh: 遊京師，跌宕詩酒，老而益貧。

translations.literal: He traveled to the capital, lived freely in poetry and wine, and grew ever poorer in old age.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to the capital, lived freely among poetry and wine, and grew ever poorer in old age.

sentences.zh: 曾燠為兩淮運使，資之歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Zeng Yan, as Transport Commissioner of the Two Huai, provided funds for his return home, and he died not long after.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yan, Transport Commissioner of the Two Huai, provided funds for his return home, and he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 妻方婉儀，亦工詩畫，好禪，號白蓮居士。

translations.literal: His wife Fang Wanyi was also skilled at poetry and painting, loved Chan, and was known as the Layman of the White Lotus.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Fang Wanyi was also skilled at poetry and painting, loved Chan, and was known as the Layman of the White Lotus.

sentences.zh: 岡，字鐵生，號蒙泉，舊為歙縣人，居錢塘，遂隸籍。

translations.literal: Gang, styled Tiesheng and known as Mengquan, was originally a man of She County; he lived in Qiantang and was registered there.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Gang, styled Tiesheng and known as Mengquan, was originally from She County but lived in Qiantang and was registered there.

sentences.zh: 負奇，不得志，寄於詩畫。

translations.literal: He bore an unusual talent, failed to realize his ambitions, and entrusted himself to poetry and painting.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted but frustrated in his ambitions, he poured himself into poetry and painting.

sentences.zh: 山水取法婁東，自成逸韵；

translations.literal: In landscape he took Loudong as his model and formed his own free resonance;
translations.idiomatic: His landscapes followed the Loudong school yet achieved a free resonance of their own;

sentences.zh: 竹石花木，超雋得元人意；

translations.literal: in bamboo, rock, flowers, and trees he was surpassingly elegant and obtained the spirit of the Yuan masters;
translations.idiomatic: his bamboo, rock, flower, and tree paintings were surpassingly elegant and captured the spirit of the Yuan masters;

sentences.zh: 四十後名益噪。

translations.literal: after forty his fame grew ever louder.
translations.idiomatic: after the age of forty his fame grew ever louder.

sentences.zh: 曾遊日本，海外估舶，懸金購其畫。

translations.literal: He once traveled to Japan, and overseas merchant ships offered gold to purchase his paintings.
translations.idiomatic: He once traveled to Japan, and overseas merchants offered gold to buy his paintings.

sentences.zh: 徵孝廉方正，辭不就。

translations.literal: Summoned as Filial and Incorrupt and Upright, he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Filial and Incorrupt and Upright, he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 岡與同縣黃易齊名。

translations.literal: Gang and Huang Yi of the same county were equally famous.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Gang and his fellow townsman Huang Yi were equally celebrated.

sentences.zh: 易父樹穀，亦工書畫。

translations.literal: Yi's father Shugu was also skilled at calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yi's father Shugu was also skilled at calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 易詳文苑傳，篤嗜金石，每以訪碑紀遊作圖，為世所重。

translations.literal: Yi is treated in detail in the Biographies of Literary Men; he was deeply devoted to epigraphy and often made paintings recording his stele visits and travels, and was valued by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yi has his own biography in the Literary Men section; deeply devoted to epigraphy, he often painted records of his stele-hunting travels and was greatly esteemed.

sentences.zh: 畫境簡淡，山左多宗之。

translations.literal: His pictorial realm was simple and plain, and many in Shandong took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: His pictorial style was spare and restrained, and many painters in Shandong followed his example.

sentences.zh: 杜字，叔美，號松壺，仁和人。

translations.literal: Du, styled Shumei and known as Songhu, was a man of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Du, styled Shumei and known as Songhu, was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 屈於下僚，曾官雲南經歷，足跡逾萬里。

translations.literal: Stifled among lower officials, he once served as Intendant of Yunnan, and his footprints exceeded ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Stifled in low office, he once served as Intendant of Yunnan and traveled more than ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 深揅畫學，摹趙伯駒、孟頫、王蒙皆神似。

translations.literal: He deeply studied painting and copied Zhao Boju, Zhao Mengfu, and Wang Meng with all resembling the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He studied painting deeply and copied Zhao Boju, Zhao Mengfu, and Wang Meng with remarkable fidelity.

sentences.zh: 間為金碧雲山，妍雅絕俗。

translations.literal: Occasionally he made blue-and-gold cloud mountains, beautiful and elegant beyond the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Occasionally he painted blue-and-gold cloud mountains of exquisite elegance beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 畫梅疏冷出趙孟堅。

translations.literal: In painting plum he was sparse and cold, surpassing Zhao Mengjian.
translations.idiomatic: His plum paintings were spare and austere, surpassing even Zhao Mengjian.

sentences.zh: 兼擅詩名。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in poetic fame.
translations.idiomatic: He was also celebrated as a poet.

sentences.zh: 著松壺畫贅、畫憶，多名論。

translations.literal: He wrote Songhu Painting Miscellany and Painting Recollections, containing many famous theories.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Songhu Painting Miscellany and Painting Recollections, both containing notable critical essays.

sentences.zh: 從兄東，字袖海，畫近惲格，名亞於杜。

translations.literal: His cousin Dong, styled Xiuhai, painted close to Yun Ge, and his fame was second to Du.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Qian Dong, styled Xiuhai, painted in a manner close to Yun Nantian, and his fame ranked below Qian Du's.

sentences.zh: 薰，字蘭坻，浙江石門人。

translations.literal: Xun, styled Lanchi, was a man of Shimen in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xun, styled Lanchi, was from Shimen in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父《呆呆》，故善畫，薰幼從父遊吳、越間，多見名跡，接耆宿，遂兼眾長。

translations.literal: His father Mei was also skilled at painting; in youth Xun followed his father traveling between Wu and Yue, saw many famous works, met venerable elders, and thus combined many strengths.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fang Mei was also skilled at painting; as a youth Xun traveled with him through Wu and Yue, saw many masterpieces, met venerable elders, and thus combined many strengths.

sentences.zh: 論畫曰：「寫生以意勝形似。」

translations.literal: On painting he said: "In life-drawing, idea surpasses resemblance in form."
translations.idiomatic: On painting he said, "In painting from life, pictorial idea should surpass resemblance in form."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「不拘難易，須雅馴。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Regardless of difficulty or ease, one must be refined and gentle."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Regardless of difficulty or ease, the work must be refined and restrained."

sentences.zh: 著山靜居論畫，以布衣終。

translations.literal: He wrote Discourse on Painting from the Mountain Quiet Hermitage and ended his life as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Discourse on Painting from the Mountain Quiet Hermitage and died a commoner.

sentences.zh: 王學浩，字椒畦，江蘇崑山人。

translations.literal: Wang Xuehao, styled Jiaoqi, was a man of Kunshan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuehao, styled Jiaoqi, was from Kunshan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年舉人。

translations.literal: A juren in the fifty-first year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He was a juren of the fifty-first year of the Qianlong reign.

sentences.zh: 幼學畫於同縣李豫德，豫德為王原祁外孫，得南宗之傳。

translations.literal: In youth he studied painting under Li Yude of the same county; Yude was Wang Yuanqi's grandson by a daughter and obtained the transmission of the Southern School.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied painting under Li Yude of the same county; Yude was Wang Yuanqi's grandson by a daughter and had inherited the Southern School tradition.

sentences.zh: 學浩溯源倪、黃，筆力蒼勁。

translations.literal: Xuehao traced his source to Ni and Huang, and his brush strength was dark and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Xuehao traced his art to Ni Zan and Huang Gongwang, and his brushwork was dark and forceful.

sentences.zh: 論畫曰：「六法，一寫字盡之。

translations.literal: On painting he said: "The Six Principles are fully contained in one word: writing.
translations.idiomatic: On painting he said, "The Six Principles are fully contained in one word: writing.

sentences.zh: 寫者，意在筆先，直追所見，雖亂頭粗服，而意趣自足。

translations.literal: To write is to have idea before the brush, directly pursuing what is seen; though the head be disheveled and the clothes coarse, the interest is sufficient in itself.
translations.idiomatic: To write is to have the idea before the brush and directly pursue what is seen; even with disheveled forms and coarse strokes, the pictorial interest suffices.

sentences.zh: 或極工麗，而氣味古雅，所謂士大夫畫也。

translations.literal: Or it may be extremely meticulous, yet with an antique and elegant flavor—this is what is called literati painting.
translations.idiomatic: Or it may be extremely refined yet retain an antique elegance—this is what is called literati painting.

sentences.zh: 否則與俗工何異？」

translations.literal: Otherwise how is it different from vulgar artisans?"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise how is it different from the work of vulgar artisans?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「畫以簡為上，雖煙客、麓台，猶未免繁碎，如大癡，真未易到。

translations.literal: He also said: "In painting, simplicity is supreme; though Yanke and Lutai still cannot avoid being overly detailed—as for Dachi, he is truly not easy to reach.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "In painting, simplicity is supreme; even Wang Shimin and Wang Yuanqi cannot avoid excessive detail—as for Huang Gongwang, he is truly hard to match.

sentences.zh: 大癡法固在荒率蒼古中求之，尤須得其不甚著力處。」

translations.literal: Dachi's method indeed lies in seeking wildness, roughness, and dark antiquity, yet one must especially obtain those places where he does not exert much force."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gongwang's method lies in seeking wildness and dark antiquity, yet one must especially grasp those passages where he exerts the least force."

sentences.zh: 時論學浩用墨，能入絹素之骨，比人深一色。

translations.literal: Contemporary critics said Xuehao's use of ink could enter the bone of silk and paper, one shade deeper than others.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Xuehao's ink could penetrate to the very bone of silk and paper, one shade deeper than others.

sentences.zh: 晚好用破筆，脫盡窠臼，畫格一變。

translations.literal: In his later years he liked to use a worn brush, cast off all conventions, and his pictorial style changed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he favored a worn brush, cast off all conventions, and his style changed entirely.

sentences.zh: 著南山論畫。

translations.literal: He wrote Discourse on Painting from the Southern Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Discourse on Painting from the Southern Mountain.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 學浩享大年，道光之季，畫苑推為尊宿。

translations.literal: Xuehao enjoyed long years; in the late Daoguang era the painting world acclaimed him as a venerable elder.
translations.idiomatic: Xuehao lived to a great age and in the late Daoguang era was acclaimed as the doyen of the painting world.

sentences.zh: 館吳中寒碧山莊劉氏，壇坫甚盛。

translations.literal: He lodged with the Liu family at Hanbi Mountain Villa in Wu, where the artistic circle flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He lodged with the Liu family at Hanbi Mountain Villa in Wu, where the artistic circle flourished greatly.

sentences.zh: 其時吳、越作者雖眾，足繼前哲名一家者，蓋寥寥焉。

translations.literal: At that time, though painters in Wu and Yue were many, those sufficient to succeed the former sages and establish a separate school were scarce indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Though painters in Wu and Yue were many at the time, few could succeed the masters of the past and establish schools of their own.

sentences.zh: 黃均，字穀原，元和人。

translations.literal: Huang Jun, styled Guyuan, was a man of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jun, styled Guyuan, was from Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 守婁東之法，盡其能事。

translations.literal: He preserved the methods of Loudong and exhausted his utmost ability.
translations.idiomatic: He preserved the Loudong methods and brought them to their fullest expression.

sentences.zh: 遊京師，法式善、秦瀛為之延譽，得官，補湖北潛江主簿，未之任。

translations.literal: Traveling to the capital, Fa Shishan and Qin Ying spread his reputation; he obtained office and was appointed Clerk of Qianjiang in Hubei, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling to the capital, Fa Shishan and Qin Ying spread his reputation; he obtained office as Clerk of Qianjiang in Hubei but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 於武昌臙脂山麓築小園，居之二十年，以吏為隱。

translations.literal: At the foot of Yanzhi Mountain in Wuchang he built a small garden and lived there twenty years, using office as a means of retirement.
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of Yanzhi Mountain in Wuchang he built a small garden and lived there for twenty years, using a minor post as cover for retirement.

sentences.zh: 畫晚而益工，於吳中稱後勁。

translations.literal: His painting grew ever more skilled in later years, and in Wu he was called a later force.
translations.idiomatic: His painting grew ever finer in his later years, and in the Wu region he was hailed as a late master.

sentences.zh: 清畫家聞人多在乾隆以前，自道光後，卓然名家者，惟湯貽汾、戴熙二人，並自有傳。

translations.literal: Qing painters renowned for fame were mostly before Qianlong; from Daoguang onward, those who stood out as famous masters were only Tang Yifen and Dai Xi, each having a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Most celebrated Qing painters flourished before the Qianlong era; after Daoguang, only Tang Yifen and Dai Xi stood out as major masters, each with his own biography.

sentences.zh: 昭文蔣寶齡著墨林今話，繼張庚畫徵錄之後，子茝生為續編，至咸豐初，視庚錄數幾倍之。

translations.literal: Jiang Baoling of Zhaowen wrote Present Talk in the Ink Forest, following Zhang Geng's Record of Painting Portents; his son Zhisheng made a sequel, and by early Xianfeng the number was nearly several times that of Geng's record.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Baoling of Zhaowen wrote Present Talk in the Ink Forest, following Zhang Geng's Record of Painting Portents; his son Zhisheng compiled a sequel, and by early Xianfeng the entries numbered nearly several times those in Geng's record.

sentences.zh: 其後光緒中，無錫秦祖詠著桐陰論畫，論次一代作者，分三編，評騭較嚴，稱略備焉。

translations.literal: Later, in the Guangxu era, Qin Zuyong of Wuxi wrote Discourse on Painting under the Tung Tree, arranging the artists of a generation in three sections with comparatively strict judgment, and it was said to be broadly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the Guangxu reign, Qin Zuyong of Wuxi wrote Discourse on Painting under the Tung Tree, surveying a generation of artists in three sections with comparatively strict judgment, and it was regarded as broadly comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 今特著其尤工者，寶齡、祖詠畫亦並有法。

translations.literal: Here we specially record those most skilled in the craft; Baoling and Zuyong's paintings also both had method.
translations.idiomatic: Here we record especially those most skilled in the craft; Baoling and Zuyong were also accomplished painters in their own right.
